title.zh: 卷三十三 列傳第二十三 范泰 荀伯子 徐廣 鄭鮮之 裴松之 何承天
title.en: Volume 33 Biographies 23: Fan Tai, Xun Bozi, Xu Guang, Zhen Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian
title.raw: 卷三十三 列傳第二十三 范泰 荀伯子 徐廣 鄭鮮之 裴松之 何承天 Volume 33 Biographies 23: Fan Tai, Xun Bozi, Xu Guang, Zhen Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十三

translations.literal: Biographies 23
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 23

sentences.zh: 范泰荀伯子徐廣鄭鮮之裴松之何承天

translations.literal: Fan Tai, Xun Bozi, Xu Guang, Zheng Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai, Xun Bozi, Xu Guang, Zheng Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, and He Chengtian

sentences.zh: 泰初為太學博士，外弟荊州刺史王忱請為天門太守。

translations.literal: Tai at first served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; his maternal cousin Wang Chen, Governor of Jing Province, requested him as Administrator of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Tai began as an erudite at the Imperial Academy. His cousin by marriage, Wang Chen, governor of Jing Province, asked that he be made administrator of Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 忱嗜酒，醉輒累旬，及醒則儼然端肅。

translations.literal: Chen loved wine; when drunk he would remain so for ten days at a stretch, yet when sober he was always dignified and grave.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was a heavy drinker who could stay drunk for weeks on end, yet when he sobered up he was every inch the upright official.

sentences.zh: 泰陳酒既傷生，所宜深誡，其言甚切。

translations.literal: Tai argued that wine harms life and ought to be sternly shunned; his words were very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Tai urged that wine ruins health and must be shunned, and spoke with unusual force.

sentences.zh: 忱嗟歎久之，曰：「見規者眾，未有若此者也。

translations.literal: Chen sighed long and said, "Many have admonished me, but none like this."
translations.idiomatic: Chen sighed for a long while and said, "Plenty of people have warned me, but never like this."

sentences.zh: 」或問忱，范泰何如謝邈，忱曰：「茂度漫。

translations.literal: " Someone asked Chen how Fan Tai compared with Xie Miao; Chen said, "Maodu is careless."
translations.idiomatic: " When someone asked Chen how Fan Tai compared with Xie Miao, Chen replied, "Maodu is too loose."

sentences.zh: 」又問何如殷覬，忱曰：「伯通易。

translations.literal: " Asked again how he compared with Yin Kai, Chen said, "Botong is too easy."
translations.idiomatic: " Asked how he compared with Yin Kai, Chen said, "Botong is too pliable."

sentences.zh: 」忱常有意立功，謂泰曰：「今城池既立，軍甲亦充，將欲掃除中原，以申宿昔之志。

translations.literal: " Chen often wished to achieve merit and told Tai, "Now that walls and ramparts stand and armor is ample, I intend to sweep the Central Plains and fulfill my long-cherished ambition."
translations.idiomatic: " Chen often dreamed of glory and told Tai, "Our defenses are up and our arms are ready. I mean to drive the barbarians from the heartland and at last fulfill my old ambition."

sentences.zh: 伯通意銳，當令擁戈前驅；

translations.literal: Botong is keen in spirit and should lead the vanguard with spear in hand;
translations.idiomatic: Botong is bold and eager—he should ride at the head of the army;

sentences.zh: 以君持重，欲相委留事，何如？

translations.literal: as you are steady and weighty, I wish to entrust you with affairs at home—what say you?
translations.idiomatic: but you are steady and reliable. I would leave the rear to you. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」泰曰：「百年逋寇，前賢挫屈者多矣，功名雖貴，鄙生所不敢謀。」

translations.literal: " Tai said, "For a hundred years the fugitive foe has made many worthies stumble; though fame and merit are precious, this humble man dares not scheme for them."
translations.idiomatic: " Tai replied, "The northern enemy has humbled great men for a century. Glory is fine, but I dare not reach for it."

sentences.zh: 會忱病卒，召泰為驃騎諮議參軍，遷中書郎。

translations.literal: When Chen fell ill and died, Tai was summoned as staff adviser to the Cavalry General-in-Chief and promoted to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen died of illness, Tai was called up as adviser to the cavalry general-in-chief and later made a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時會稽世子元顯專權，內外百官請假，不復表聞，唯簽元顯而已。

translations.literal: At that time the Heir of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, monopolized power; officials within and without who requested leave no longer submitted memorials to the throne, but only countersigned for Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kuaiji's heir, Yuanxian, held sole power. Officials seeking leave no longer reported to the throne—they merely countersigned Yuanxian's approval.

sentences.zh: 泰言以為非宜，元顯不納。

translations.literal: Tai said this was improper; Yuanxian did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Tai protested that this was wrong; Yuanxian ignored him.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，襲爵陽遂鄉侯。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's death, and inherited the title Marquis of Yangsui Township.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father and inherited the marquisate of Yangsui township.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔晉，使御史中丞祖台之奏泰及前司徒左長史王准之、輔國將軍司馬珣之並居喪無禮，泰坐廢，徙丹徒。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted Jin, he had the Censor-in-Chief Zu Taizhi impeach Tai, together with the former Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Wang Zhunzhi and the General Who Supports the State Sima Xunzhi, for breaches of mourning ritual; Tai was dismissed and exiled to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: While Huan Xuan controlled Jin, the censor-in-chief Zu Taizhi impeached Tai, along with Wang Zhunzhi and Sima Xunzhi, for violating mourning rites. Tai was stripped of office and sent to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝義旗建，累遷黃門侍郎、御史中丞，坐議殷祠事謬，白衣領職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised the banner of righteousness, Tai was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Censor-in-Chief; for an error in deliberating the Yin ancestral rites he served in plain clothes while retaining office.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu raised his righteous banner, Tai rose to attendant at the yellow gate and censor-in-chief. A mistake in debate over the Yin ancestral rites cost him his robes of office, though he kept the post.

sentences.zh: 出為東陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 曆侍中，度支尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as attendant-in-ordinary and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時僕射陳郡謝混後進知名，武帝嘗從容問混：「泰名輩誰比？

translations.literal: At that time the Vice Director Xie Hun of Chen Commandery was famed among the younger generation; the Emperor once asked Hun at leisure, "To whom in reputation and generation may Tai be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hun of Chen Commandery was then the best-known man of the rising generation. The emperor once asked him casually, "Whom does Fan Tai resemble in rank and reputation?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「王元太一流人也。

translations.literal: " He answered, "A man of Wang Yuantai's class."
translations.idiomatic: " Hun answered, "Men like Wang Yuantai."

sentences.zh: 」徙為太常。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was transferred to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 初，司徒道規無子，養文帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Minister of Works Daogui had no sons and adopted Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Minister of Works Daogui had no sons and had adopted Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 及道規薨，以兄道憐第二子義慶為嗣。

translations.literal: When Daogui died, his elder brother Daolian's second son Yiqing was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Daogui died, his elder brother Daolian's second son Yiqing became the heir.

sentences.zh: 武帝以道規素愛文帝，又令居重。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Daogui had always loved Emperor Wen, also ordered him to hold the senior line.
translations.idiomatic: Because Daogui had always favored Emperor Wen, the emperor also kept him in the senior line of succession.

sentences.zh: 及道規追封南郡公，應以先華容縣公賜文帝。

translations.literal: When Daogui was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Nan Commandery, the former Marquisate of Huarong County ought to have been granted to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Daogui was posthumously made duke of Nan Commandery, the old Huarong county marquisate should have passed to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 泰議以為「禮無二主」，由是文帝還本屬。

translations.literal: Tai argued that "ritual admits no two lords," and on this basis Emperor Wen returned to his original house.
translations.idiomatic: Tai argued that "ritual knows no two lords," and on that ground Emperor Wen reverted to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 後加散騎常侍，為尚書兼司空，與右僕射袁湛授宋公九錫，隨軍到洛陽。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made Supernumerary Regular Attendant, served as Minister of the Interior concurrently with Minister of Works, and with the Right Vice Director Yuan Zhan invested the Duke of Song with the Nine Bestowments, following the army to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made supernumerary regular attendant, served as minister of the interior and concurrently minister of works, and with Yuan Zhan invested the Duke of Song with the Nine Bestowments on the march to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 武帝還彭城，與泰登城。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to Pengcheng, he climbed the wall with Tai.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Pengcheng, the emperor climbed the city wall with Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰有足疾，特命乘輿。

translations.literal: Tai had an ailment of the foot and was specially ordered to ride in the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tai had trouble with his feet and was specially allowed to ride in the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 泰好酒，不拘小節，通率任心。

translations.literal: Tai loved wine, did not bind himself to small proprieties, and was open and free in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Tai loved wine, cared little for petty etiquette, and lived with open, unforced ease.

sentences.zh: 雖公坐，笑言不異私室，武帝甚賞愛之。

translations.literal: Even in public audience his laughter and speech were no different from those in private; the Emperor greatly prized and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Even at court his laughter and talk were no different from those at home, and the emperor delighted in him.

sentences.zh: 然短於為政，故不得在政事官。

translations.literal: Yet he was short in governing affairs, and therefore could not hold an office of state policy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was weak in administration, and so never held a post in active governance.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，議建國學，以泰領國子祭酒，泰上表陳獎進之道。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, the founding of the National Academy was debated; Tai was put in charge as Director of the National University, and submitted a memorial setting forth the way to encourage and advance learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, plans were made for a national academy. Tai was made director of the national university and submitted a memorial on how learning ought to be encouraged.

sentences.zh: 時學竟不立。

translations.literal: At the time the academy was never established.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the academy was never built.

sentences.zh: 又言事者多以錢貨減少，國用不足，欲更造五銖。

translations.literal: Again, memorialists often said that coin had diminished and state revenue was insufficient, and wished to recast the five-zhu coin.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists also complained that coin was scarce and the treasury short, and proposed recasting the five-zhu coin.

sentences.zh: 泰又諫曰：

translations.literal: Tai again remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tai remonstrated again:

sentences.zh: 臣聞為國拯弊，莫若務本。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that to rescue a state from decline, nothing surpasses attending to the root.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to rescue a state from decline, nothing surpasses tending the root.

sentences.zh: 「百姓不足，君孰與足」，未有人貧而國富，本不足而末有餘者也。

translations.literal: "When the people are insufficient, with whom shall the ruler be sufficient?" Never yet has a people been poor while the state was rich, or the root insufficient while the branches had surplus.
translations.idiomatic: "When the people lack, how can the ruler have enough?" No people were ever poor while the state grew rich, nor the root withered while the branches flourished.

sentences.zh: 故囊漏貯中，識者不吝，反裘負薪，存毛實難。

translations.literal: Hence a leak in the purse still fills the storehouse—wise men do not begrudge it; to wear the fur inside out while carrying firewood preserves the hide but truly harms the task.
translations.idiomatic: A leak in the purse still fills the storehouse—wise men do not begrudge the loss; to wear the fur inside out while carrying firewood saves the pelt but ruins the work.

sentences.zh: 王者不言有無，諸侯不說多少，食祿之家，不與百姓爭利。

translations.literal: The king does not speak of having or lacking; feudal lords do not discuss more or less; households on salary do not contend for profit with the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Kings do not count their stores aloud; lords do not haggle over sums; salaried houses do not wrest profit from the people.

sentences.zh: 故拔葵所以明政，織蒲謂之不仁。

translations.literal: Hence plucking the mallow made policy clear, and weaving rushes was called inhumane.
translations.idiomatic: Plucking mallow in a minister's garden clarified public duty; weaving rushes for private gain was called inhumane.

sentences.zh: 是以貴賤有章，職分無爽。

translations.literal: Therefore high and low had their ranks, and offices their proper measure without deviation.
translations.idiomatic: High and low had their ranks, and every office its proper measure.

sentences.zh: 今之所憂，在農人尚寡，倉廩未充，轉運無已，資食者眾，家無私積，難以禦荒耳。

translations.literal: What should now be feared is that farmers are still few, granaries are not full, transport never ceases, those who live on provisions are many, and households have no private stores—hardly enough to meet famine.
translations.idiomatic: What we should fear is too few farmers, half-empty granaries, endless transport, too many mouths on public grain, and households with no private stores—hardly enough to survive famine.

sentences.zh: 夫貨存貿易，不在少多，昔日之貴，今者之賤，彼此共之，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Goods exist for exchange; it lies not in more or less. What was costly yesterday is cheap today—both sides share in it; the principle is one.
translations.idiomatic: Money exists for exchange, not for counting. What was costly yesterday is cheap today—the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 但令官人均通，則無患不足。

translations.literal: Only let official and private circulation be even, and there will be no fear of insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: If circulation is even between public and private purses, scarcity need not be feared.

sentences.zh: 若使必資貨廣以收國用者，則龜貝之屬，自古所行。

translations.literal: If one must rely on broadening goods to fill state use, then tortoise shells and cowrie shells have been used since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: If the state must widen the money supply to fill its coffers, tortoise shells and cowries were used in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 尋銅之為器，在用也博矣，鍾律所通者遠，機衡所揆者大，夏鼎負圖，實冠眾瑞，晉鐸呈象，亦啟休征。

translations.literal: Consider copper as material for vessels: its uses are vast; bells and pitch-pipes reach far; scales and measures measure greatly; the Xia cauldron bearing the chart truly crowns all omens; the Jin bell displaying its image also opened an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Copper serves countless uses—bells and pitch-pipes, scales and measures; the Xia cauldron bearing the chart crowned all omens, and the Jin bell displaying its image opened an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 器有要用，則貴賤同資，物有適宜，則家國共急。

translations.literal: When a vessel has essential use, high and low alike rely on it; when a thing suits its purpose, family and state alike need it urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When a vessel is truly needed, rich and poor alike depend on it; when a thing fits its use, household and state alike depend on it.

sentences.zh: 今毀必資之器，而為無施之錢，於貨則功不補勞，在用則君人俱困，校之以實，損多益少。

translations.literal: Now to destroy vessels on which one must rely and make coins of no use—in goods the labor will not repay the cost, in use ruler and people alike will be distressed; measured by fact, loss exceeds gain.
translations.idiomatic: To destroy indispensable vessels and mint useless coin wastes labor, burdens ruler and people alike, and by any honest measure costs more than it yields.

sentences.zh: 伏願思可久之道，探欲速之情，弘山海之納，擇芻牧之說。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to ponder the way that endures, probe the urge for speed, enlarge the acceptance of mountain and sea, and choose counsel from the herdsman.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to seek what endures, resist haste, accept counsel from every quarter, and heed even the herdsman's word.

sentences.zh: 景平初，加位特進，明年致仕，解國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingping era he was given the special rank of Special Advance; the next year he retired and resigned the directorship of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingping he was given special advance rank; the next year he retired and gave up the national university.

sentences.zh: 少帝在位，多諸愆失，泰上封事極諫。

translations.literal: While the Deposed Emperor reigned, there were many faults; Tai submitted sealed memorials remonstrating to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Under the deposed emperor's reign Tai submitted sealed memorials of fierce remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 少帝雖不能納，亦不加譴。

translations.literal: Though the Deposed Emperor could not accept them, he also did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor could not accept them, yet did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮等與泰素不平，及廬陵王義真、少帝見害，泰謂所親曰：「吾觀古今多矣，未有受遺顧托，而嗣君見殺，賢王嬰戮者也。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and others had long been at odds with Tai; when Prince of Luling Yizhen and the Deposed Emperor were killed, Tai told those close to him, "I have seen much of past and present, yet never one who received a deathbed charge and trust, only to see the heir slain and worthy princes put to the sword."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and others had long disliked Tai. When Prince Yizhen of Luling and the deposed emperor were killed, Tai told his intimates, "I have read much history, yet never of a regent entrusted at death whose heir was murdered and a worthy prince slaughtered."

sentences.zh: 」元嘉二年，泰表賀元正並陳旱災，多所獎勸。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Yuanjia, Tai submitted a memorial congratulating the New Year and stating drought disaster, with much encouragement and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: " In Yuanjia 2 Tai submitted a New Year congratulation that also described drought and offered much encouragement and warning.

sentences.zh: 拜表遂輕舟游東陽，任心行止，不關朝廷。

translations.literal: After presenting the memorial he took a light boat to wander in Dongyang, going and stopping as his heart wished, without regard to court.
translations.idiomatic: After presenting it he took a light boat to wander in Dongyang, going where he pleased without regard to court.

sentences.zh: 有司劾奏之，文帝不問。

translations.literal: The responsible officials impeached him; Emperor Wen did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached him; Emperor Wen took no notice.

sentences.zh: 時文帝雖當陽親覽，而羨之等猶執重權，泰復上表論得失，言及執事。

translations.literal: At that time though Emperor Wen personally attended to affairs, Xu Xianzhi and others still held heavy power; Tai again submitted a memorial discussing gains and losses, touching on those in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Wen now ruled in person, Xu Xianzhi and his faction still held power. Tai submitted another memorial on policy, naming those in charge.

sentences.zh: 諸子禁之，表竟不奏。

translations.literal: His sons forbade it, and the memorial was never presented.
translations.idiomatic: His sons stopped him, and the memorial never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 三年，羨之伏誅，進位侍中、左光祿大夫、國子祭酒，領江夏王師，特進如故。

translations.literal: In the third year Xu Xianzhi was executed; Tai was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of the Palace, Director of the National University, tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia, with Special Advance as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xu Xianzhi was executed. Tai was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary, left grand master of the palace, director of the national university, and tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia, retaining special advance rank.

sentences.zh: 上以泰先朝舊臣，恩禮甚重。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Tai was an old minister of the former reign, showed him very heavy favor and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tai was an old minister of the previous reign, the emperor treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 以有腳疾，宴見之日，特聽乘輿到坐。

translations.literal: Because he had an ailment of the leg, on days of banquet audience he was specially permitted to ride in the carriage to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his leg ailment, on banquet days he was allowed to ride the carriage right to his seat.

sentences.zh: 所陳時事，上每優容之。

translations.literal: On current affairs that he presented, the Emperor always received him with generous forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he raised about current affairs, the emperor always heard him with generous forbearance.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，旱蝗，又上表言：「有蝗之處，縣官多課人捕之，無益于枯苗，有傷於殺害。

translations.literal: That autumn there was drought and locusts; he again submitted a memorial saying, "Where there are locusts, district officials often levy people to catch them—this does no good to withered seedlings and only adds to slaughter."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn drought and locusts struck. He submitted another memorial: "Where locusts appear, officials levy people to catch them—useless for withered crops, and only more killing."

sentences.zh: 又女人被宥，由來尚矣，謝晦婦女猶在尚方，匹婦一至，亦能有所感激。

translations.literal: Again, pardon for women has been honored from old; Xie Hui's women are still in the palace workshops—a single common woman restored can also stir feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Pardoning women has long been honored practice. Xie Hui's women still languish in the palace workshops—even one ordinary woman restored can move hearts."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上乃原謝晦婦女。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was presented, the Emperor then pardoned Xie Hui's women.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor pardoned Xie Hui's women.

sentences.zh: 時司徒王弘輔政，泰謂弘曰：「彭城王，帝之次弟，宜征還入朝，共參朝政。

translations.literal: At that time the Minister of Works Wang Hong assisted in government; Tai told Hong, "The Prince of Pengcheng is the Emperor's next younger brother and ought to be summoned back to court to join in governing."
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Works Wang Hong was regent, Tai told him, "The Prince of Pengcheng is the emperor's next younger brother. Summon him to court to share in governance."

sentences.zh: 」弘納其言。

translations.literal: " Hong accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong took his advice.

sentences.zh: 時旱災未已，加以疾疫，泰又上表有所勸誡。

translations.literal: At that time drought disaster had not yet ceased, and pestilence was added; Tai again submitted a memorial with admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Drought had not yet ended and pestilence had come; Tai submitted another memorial of warning.

sentences.zh: 泰博覽篇籍，好為文章，愛獎後生，孜孜無倦。

translations.literal: Tai read widely in books, loved to write, delighted in encouraging the young, and was tireless.
translations.idiomatic: Tai read widely, loved writing, delighted in encouraging the young, and never tired of it.

sentences.zh: 撰古今善言二十四篇及文集傳於世。

translations.literal: He compiled twenty-four chapters of fine words ancient and modern, and a collected works that circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled twenty-four chapters of fine words from antiquity and his own age, and a collected works that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 暮年事佛甚精，於宅西立只洹精舍。

translations.literal: In his later years he devoted himself deeply to Buddhism and built the Jihuan Hermitage west of his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he devoted himself to Buddhism and built the Jihuan Hermitage west of his house.

sentences.zh: 五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 初議贈開府，殷景仁曰：「泰素望不重，不可擬議台司。

translations.literal: At first it was debated to posthumously grant him the opening of a grand office; Yin Jingren said, "Tai's standing was never weighty; he cannot be compared to the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: At first there was talk of posthumously opening a grand office for him. Yin Jingren said, "Tai's standing was never great enough to rank with the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 」竟不果。

translations.literal: " In the end it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end it did not happen.

sentences.zh: 及葬，王弘撫棺哭曰：「君生平重殷鐵，今以此為報。

translations.literal: At the burial Wang Hong stroked the coffin and wept, saying, "In life you valued Yin Tie; now this is your repayment."
translations.idiomatic: At the burial Wang Hong stroked the coffin and wept: "You valued Yin Tie all your life—this is your repayment."

sentences.zh: 」追贈車騎將軍，諡曰宣侯。

translations.literal: " He was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with the posthumous title Marquis Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He was posthumously made general of chariots and cavalry, with the posthumous name Marquis Xuan.

sentences.zh: 第四子曄最知名。

translations.literal: The fourth son Ye was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth son Ye was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 曄字蔚宗，母如廁產之，額為磚所傷，故以磚為小字。

translations.literal: Ye, styled Weizong, was born when his mother went to the privy; his forehead was injured by a brick, and therefore Brick was his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, styled Weizong, was born when his mother went to the privy. A brick struck his forehead, so Brick was his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 出繼從伯弘之，後襲封武興縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He went out to be adopted by his father's elder brother's son Hongzhi, and later inherited the fifth-rank marquisate of Wuxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was given in adoption to his father's cousin Hongzhi and later inherited the fifth-rank marquisate of Wuxing county.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善為文章，能隸書，曉音律。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled at writing, could write clerical script, and understood music.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning, wrote well, mastered clerical script, and understood music.

sentences.zh: 為秘書丞，父憂去職。

translations.literal: He served as Secretary Assistant and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretary assistant and left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為征南大將軍檀道濟司馬，領新蔡太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became staff secretary to the General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji and concurrently Administrator of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became staff secretary to Tan Daoji, general who conquers the south, and concurrently governor of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became senior clerk in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，彭城太妃薨，將葬，祖夕，僚故並集東府，曄與司徒左西屬王深及弟司徒祭酒廣夜中酣飲，開北牖聽輓歌為樂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia the Grand Consort of Pengcheng died; when burial was imminent, on the eve of the procession all colleagues and old associates gathered at the eastern residence. Ye, with Wang Shen, Left Western Attendant of the Minister of Works, and his younger brother Guang, libationer of the Minister of Works, drank deep into the night, opened the north window, and listened to dirges for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 9 the grand consort of Pengcheng died. On the eve of the funeral procession, colleagues gathered at the eastern residence. Ye, with Wang Shen and his brother Guang, drank deep into the night, opened the north window, and listened to dirges for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康大怒，左遷宣城太守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang was greatly angered and demoted him to Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng was furious and demoted him to governor of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 不得志，乃刪眾家後漢書為一家之作，至於屈伸榮辱之際，未嘗不致意焉。

translations.literal: Frustrated in his ambitions, he then edited the various family histories of the Later Han into a single work; in passages of rise and fall, honor and shame, he never failed to invest feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated, he edited the various Later Han histories into one work; in every passage of rise and fall, honor and shame, he invested his feeling.

sentences.zh: 遷長沙王義欣鎮軍長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to senior staff secretary to Prince Yixin of Changsha, commanding general on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to senior staff secretary to Prince Yixin of Changsha, commanding general on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 兄暠為宜都太守，嫡母隨暠在官亡，報之以疾，曄不時奔赴。

translations.literal: His elder brother Hao was Administrator of Yidu; his stepmother followed Hao and died in office. He reported illness and Ye did not go promptly.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Hao was governor of Yidu; his stepmother followed Hao and died in office. Ye reported illness and did not go promptly.

sentences.zh: 及行，又攜伎妾自隨，為御史中丞劉損所奏。

translations.literal: When he did go, he again took singing girls and concubines with him, and was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief Liu Sun.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally went, he took singing girls and concubines with him and was impeached by Liu Sun, censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 文帝愛其才，不罪也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen loved his talent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen valued his talent and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，累遷左衛將軍、太子詹事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Left Guard and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he rose to general of the left guard and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 曄長不滿七尺，肥黑，禿眉鬢，善彈琵琶，能為新聲。

translations.literal: Ye was less than seven feet tall, fat and dark, with bald brows and temples; he was skilled at playing the pipa and could compose new tunes.
translations.idiomatic: Ye stood under seven feet, fat and dark, with bald brows and temples. He played the pipa beautifully and composed new tunes.

sentences.zh: 上欲聞之，屢諷以微旨，曄偽若不曉，終不肯為。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to hear them and repeatedly hinted; Ye pretended not to understand and in the end would not play.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to hear them and hinted repeatedly; Ye feigned not to understand and never played.

sentences.zh: 上嘗宴飲勸適，謂曄曰：「我欲歌，卿可彈。

translations.literal: The Emperor once feasted and drank until tipsy and said to Ye, "I wish to sing; you may play."
translations.idiomatic: Once at a tipsy feast the emperor said to Ye, "I want to sing—you play."

sentences.zh: 」曄乃奉旨。

translations.literal: " Ye then obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: " Ye obeyed.

sentences.zh: 上歌既畢，曄亦止弦。

translations.literal: When the Emperor finished singing, Ye also stopped the strings.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor finished singing, Ye stopped the strings.

sentences.zh: 初，魯國孔熙先博學有從橫才志，文史星算，無不兼善，為員外散騎侍郎，不為時知，久不得調。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kong Xixian of Lu was learned and had talent for horizontal persuasion; literature, history, stars, and calculation—none he did not combine and excel in. He was Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant, unknown to the age, long without transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kong Xixian of Lu was learned and possessed a persuader's wit; literature, history, astronomy, and calculation—he mastered them all. He was supernumerary regular cavalry attendant, unknown to his age, long without promotion.

sentences.zh: 初，熙先父默之為廣州刺史，以贓貨下廷尉，大將軍彭城王義康保持之，故免。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xixian's father Mozhi was Governor of Guang Province; for embezzlement he was sent to the Minister of Justice; the Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang protected him, and therefore he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian's father Mozhi had been governor of Guang Province. For embezzlement he was sent to the minister of justice; Prince Yikang of Pengcheng protected him and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 及義康被黜，熙先密懷報效，以曄意志不滿，欲引之，無因進說。

translations.literal: When Yikang was removed, Xixian secretly harbored repayment; because Ye was discontent in mind, he wished to draw him in but had no opening to speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang fell, Xixian secretly planned repayment. Ye was discontent, and Xixian wished to draw him in but found no opening.

sentences.zh: 曄甥謝綜雅為曄所知，熙先藉嶺南遺財，家甚富足，乃傾身事綜。

translations.literal: Ye's nephew Xie Zongya was well known to Ye; Xixian, relying on inherited wealth from the south, was very rich in household, and therefore devoted himself to Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's nephew Xie Zongya was close to him. Xixian, rich on inherited southern wealth, devoted himself to Zong.

sentences.zh: 始與綜諸弟共博，故為拙行，以物輸之，情意稍款。

translations.literal: At first he gambled with Zong and his brothers, deliberately playing badly and losing goods to them; affection gradually grew warm.
translations.idiomatic: At first he gambled with Zong and his brothers, deliberately playing badly and losing goods until affection warmed.

sentences.zh: 綜乃引熙先與曄戲，熙先故為不敵，前後輸曄物甚多。

translations.literal: Zong then introduced Xixian to play with Ye; Xixian deliberately played as if no match and before and after lost many goods to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zong introduced Xixian to play with Ye. Xixian deliberately lost again and again, yielding many goods.

sentences.zh: 曄既利其財寶，又愛其文藝，遂與申莫逆之好。

translations.literal: Ye both profited from his wealth and loved his literary talent, and therefore formed with him the closest friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Ye profited from his wealth and loved his literary gifts, and they became inseparable friends.

sentences.zh: 熙先始以微言動曄，曄不回。

translations.literal: Xixian at first moved Ye with subtle words; Ye did not turn.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian at first moved Ye with subtle words; Ye would not turn.

sentences.zh: 曄素有閨庭論議，朝野所知，故門胄雖華，而國家不與姻，以此激之曰：「丈人若謂朝廷相待厚者，何故不與丈人婚，為是門戶不得邪？

translations.literal: Ye had long had household debates known to court and country; though his gate was noble, the state did not marry with him. Xixian used this to provoke him, saying, "If you say the court treats you generously, why does it not marry with you—is your house not good enough?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye's household debates were known throughout court and country. Though his house was noble, the throne would not marry with it. Xixian provoked him: "If the court treats you so well, why won't it marry with you—is your house not good enough?"

sentences.zh: 人作犬豕相遇，而丈人欲為之死，不亦惑乎。

translations.literal: When men meet like dogs and pigs, yet you wish to die for them—is that not deluded?
translations.idiomatic: Men meet like dogs and pigs, yet you would die for them—is that not madness?

sentences.zh: 」曄默然不答，其意乃定。

translations.literal: " Ye was silent and did not answer; his mind was then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: " Ye said nothing; his mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 時曄與沈演之並為上所知待，每被見多同，曄若先至，必待演之，演之先至，常獨被引，曄又以此為怨。

translations.literal: At that time Ye and Shen Yanzhi were both known and favored by the Emperor; when summoned they were often together. If Ye arrived first he always waited for Yanzhi; if Yanzhi arrived first he was often summoned alone—Ye again resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and Shen Yanzhi were both favored. When summoned together, if Ye arrived first he waited for Yanzhi; if Yanzhi arrived first he was often summoned alone. Ye resented this.

sentences.zh: 曄累經義康府佐，見待素厚，及宣城之授，意好乖離。

translations.literal: Ye had repeatedly served in Yikang's staff and had always been treated generously; with the appointment to Xuancheng, their affection turned estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had long served Yikang's staff and been treated generously; the Xuancheng appointment turned their affection cold.

sentences.zh: 綜為義康大將軍記室參軍，隨鎮豫章。

translations.literal: Zong was staff recorder to Yikang as grand general and followed him to garrison at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was staff recorder to Grand General Yikang and followed him to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 綜還，申義康意於曄，求解晚隙，復敦往好。

translations.literal: When Zong returned he conveyed Yikang's intent to Ye, asking to dissolve the late breach and restore former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong returned he conveyed Yikang's wish to heal the breach and restore old friendship.

sentences.zh: 曄既有逆謀，欲探時旨，乃言於上曰：「臣曆觀前史二漢故事，諸蕃王政以妖詛幸災，便正大逆之罰。

translations.literal: Ye, having a treasonous plot, wished to probe the times and therefore said to the Emperor, "Your servant has reviewed the precedents of the two Han dynasties: when feudal princes were punished for sorcery and rejoicing at disaster, they were immediately charged with great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Plotting treason, Ye wished to probe the throne and said, "I have reviewed Han precedents: when princes were punished for sorcery and rejoicing at disaster, they were charged at once with great treason.

sentences.zh: 況義康奸心釁跡，彰著遐邇，而至今無恙，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: How much more when Yikang's treacherous heart and marks of guilt are clear far and near, yet to this day goes unharmed—your servant is privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang's treachery is plain far and near, yet he goes unharmed—I am baffled.

sentences.zh: 且大梗常存，將成亂階。

translations.literal: Moreover a great obstruction constantly remains and will become the steps of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: A great obstruction remains and will become the steps of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」上不納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 熙先素善天文，云：「文帝必以非道晏駕，當由骨肉相殘。

translations.literal: Xixian had long been skilled at astronomy and said, "Emperor Wen will surely die by violence and it will come from kin killing kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian, skilled in astronomy, said, "Emperor Wen will die by violence, and kin will kill kin.

sentences.zh: 江州應出天子。

translations.literal: Jiang Province should produce the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Province will produce the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」以為義康當之。

translations.literal: " He thought Yikang would be the one.
translations.idiomatic: " He thought Yikang would be the one.

sentences.zh: 綜父述亦為義康所遇，綜弟約又是義康女夫，故文帝使綜隨從南上。

translations.literal: Zong's father Shu had also been favored by Yikang; Zong's younger brother Yue was also Yikang's son-in-law; therefore Emperor Wen had Zong follow the southward journey.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's father Shu had been favored by Yikang; Zong's brother Yue was Yikang's son-in-law. The emperor had Zong follow the southward journey.

sentences.zh: 既為熙先獎說，亦有酬報之心。

translations.literal: Having been urged by Xixian, he also had a heart to repay favor.
translations.idiomatic: Urged by Xixian, he too wished to repay favor.

sentences.zh: 廣州人周靈甫有家兵部曲，熙先以六十萬錢與之，使于廣州合兵。

translations.literal: Zhou Lingfu of Guang Province had household troops and retainers; Xixian gave him six hundred thousand cash to gather soldiers at Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lingfu of Guang Province had household troops. Xixian gave him six hundred thousand cash to raise soldiers there.

sentences.zh: 靈甫一去不反。

translations.literal: Lingfu went and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu went and never returned.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府史仲承祖，義康舊所信念，屢銜命下都，亦潛結腹心，規有異志。

translations.literal: Zhong Chengzu, clerk of the Grand General's residence, had long been trusted by Yikang and repeatedly carried orders to the capital; he also secretly joined confidants and plotted divergent intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chengzu, clerk in the grand general's residence, had long been trusted by Yikang and often carried orders to the capital. He too secretly joined confidants and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 聞熙先有誠，密相結納。

translations.literal: Hearing Xixian's sincerity, he secretly joined and attached himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Xixian's resolve, he secretly joined him.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹徐湛之素為義康所愛，雖為舅甥，恩過子弟，承祖因此結事湛之，告以密計。

translations.literal: Xu Zhanzhi, Governor of Danyang, had long been loved by Yikang; though nephew by marriage, his favor exceeded that of sons and nephews; Chengzu therefore joined with Zhanzhi through this and told him the secret plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanzhi, governor of Danyang, had long been loved by Yikang. Though nephew by marriage, he was favored like a son. Chengzu joined Zhanzhi and revealed the plot.

sentences.zh: 承祖南下，申義康意于蕭思話及曄，云：「本欲與蕭結婚，恨始意不果。

translations.literal: Chengzu going south conveyed Yikang's intent to Xiao Sihua and Ye, saying, "I originally wished to marry with Xiao but regret the first intent did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu going south conveyed Yikang's intent to Xiao Sihua and Ye: "I meant to ally with Xiao by marriage, but the first plan failed.

sentences.zh: 與範本情不薄，中間相失，傍人為之耳。」

translations.literal: With Fan the original feeling was not thin; the middle loss was others' doing."
translations.idiomatic: With Fan the bond was never thin; the breach was others' doing."

sentences.zh: 有法略道人先為義康所養，粗被知待。

translations.literal: There was the Daoist Falüe, formerly raised by Yikang and roughly treated with some regard.
translations.idiomatic: There was the Daoist Falüe, once raised by Yikang and treated with some regard.

sentences.zh: 又有王國寺法靜尼出入義康家內，皆感激舊恩，規相拯拔，並與熙先往來。

translations.literal: There was also the nun Fajing of Wangguo Temple who went in and out of Yikang's household; all were moved by old favor and plotted mutual rescue, and all associated with Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: The nun Fajing of Wangguo Temple also came and went in Yikang's house. All were moved by old favor and plotted rescue, and all associated with Xixian.

sentences.zh: 使法略罷道。

translations.literal: They had Falüe leave the Dao.
translations.idiomatic: They had Falüe leave the Dao.

sentences.zh: 法略本姓孫，改名景玄，以為臧質寧遠參軍。

translations.literal: Falüe's original surname was Sun; he changed his name to Jingxuan and was made staff officer to Zang Zhi, pacifier of the far frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Falüe's original surname was Sun. He renamed himself Jingxuan and became staff officer to Zang Zhi, pacifier of the far frontier.

sentences.zh: 熙先善療病兼能診脈，法靜尼妹夫許耀領隊在台，宿衛殿省，嘗有疾，因法靜尼就熙先乞療得損，因成周旋。

translations.literal: Xixian was skilled at treating illness and also at pulse diagnosis; Xu Yao, brother-in-law of Fajing the nun, commanded a guard unit at the capital, guarding the palace halls; he once had an illness and through Fajing the nun asked Xixian to treat him and was improved, and thus formed association.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian was skilled at medicine and pulse. Xu Yao, Fajing's brother-in-law, commanded a guard unit at the palace. Ill once, he was treated through Fajing and improved, and they became associates.

sentences.zh: 熙先以耀膽幹，因告逆謀，耀許為內應。

translations.literal: Xixian, because Yao was bold and capable, therefore told him the treasonous plot; Yao agreed to be the inside response.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yao bold and capable, Xixian told him the plot; Yao agreed to respond from within.

sentences.zh: 豫章胡藩子遵世與法靜甚款，亦密相酬和。

translations.literal: Zunshi, son of Hu Fan of Yuzhang, was very intimate with Fajing and also secretly joined in mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi, son of Hu Fan of Yuzhang, was intimate with Fajing and secretly joined the plot.

sentences.zh: 法靜尼南上，熙先遣婢采藻隨之，付以箋書，陳說圖讖。

translations.literal: Fajing the nun went south; Xixian sent the maid Caizao to follow her and gave her letters setting forth portents and charts.
translations.idiomatic: Fajing went south. Xixian sent the maid Caizao after her with letters of portents and charts.

sentences.zh: 法靜還，義康餉熙先銅匕銅鑷袍段棋奩等物。

translations.literal: When Fajing returned, Yikang sent Xixian copper spoons, copper tweezers, robe cloth, and a chess case.
translations.idiomatic: When Fajing returned, Yikang sent Xixian copper spoons, tweezers, robe cloth, and a chess case.

sentences.zh: 熙先慮事泄，酖采藻殺之。

translations.literal: Xixian feared the affair would leak and poisoned Caizao to death.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Xixian poisoned Caizao to death.

sentences.zh: 湛之又謂曄等：「臧質見與異常，質與蕭思話款密，二人並受大將軍眷遇，必無異同，不憂兵力不足，但當勿失機耳。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi again told Ye and the others, "Zang Zhi's treatment of me is extraordinary; Zhi and Xiao Sihua are close, and both received the Grand General's favor—they will surely not differ; do not worry that troops are insufficient, only do not miss the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi told Ye and the others, "Zang Zhi treats me exceptionally. He and Xiao Sihua are close, both favored by the grand general—they will not waver. Do not fear insufficient troops; only do not miss the moment."

sentences.zh: 」乃備相署置：湛之為撫軍將軍、揚州刺史，曄中軍將軍、南徐州刺史，熙先左衛將軍。

translations.literal: " They then fully arranged appointments: Zhanzhi as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Yang Province; Ye as General of the Central Army and Governor of South Xuzhou; Xixian as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " They arranged appointments: Zhanzhi as pacifying general and governor of Yang Province; Ye as central army general and governor of South Xuzhou; Xixian as left guard general.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆有選擬。

translations.literal: The rest all had selections proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The rest all had posts assigned.

sentences.zh: 凡素所不善及不附義康者，又有別簿，併入死目。

translations.literal: All whom they disliked and all who did not attach to Yikang were also in a separate register, together entering the death list.
translations.idiomatic: Those they disliked and all who did not follow Yikang went on a separate register—the death list.

sentences.zh: 熙先使弟休先豫為檄文，言賊臣趙伯符肆兵犯蹕，禍流儲宰，乃奉戴義康。

translations.literal: Xixian had his younger brother Xiuxian draft the proclamation in advance, saying the traitor minister Zhao Bofu wantonly raised troops and violated the imperial progress, disaster flowing to the heir-preserver, and therefore they would uphold Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian had his brother Xiuxian draft the proclamation: the traitor Zhao Bofu had raised troops against the imperial progress, disaster had reached the heir-preserver, and they would uphold Yikang.

sentences.zh: 又以既為大事，宜須義康意旨，乃作義康與湛之書，宣示同黨。

translations.literal: Again, since the great affair was already decided, Yikang's intent must be obtained; he therefore made a letter from Yikang to Zhanzhi and displayed it to the party.
translations.idiomatic: Since the great affair was decided, they needed Yikang's intent. Xixian forged a letter from Yikang to Zhanzhi and showed it to the party.

sentences.zh: 二十二年九月，征北將軍衡陽王義季、右將軍南平王鑠出鎮，上于武帳岡祖道。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year, the General Who Conquers the North Prince of Hengyang Yiji and the General of the Right Prince of Nanping Shuo went out to garrison; the Emperor saw them off at Wuzhang Hill.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year, Prince Yiji of Hengyang and Prince Shuo of Nanping went out to garrison. The emperor saw them off at Wuzhang Hill.

sentences.zh: 曄等期以其日為亂，許耀侍上，扣刀以目曄，曄不敢視，俄而坐散，差互不得發。

translations.literal: Ye and the others fixed on that day for disorder; Yao attended the Emperor, touched his knife and signaled Ye with his eyes; Ye dared not look; soon the sitting dispersed and the timing missed—they could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and the others chose that day for the rising. Yao attended the emperor, touched his knife, and signaled Ye; Ye dared not look. The assembly broke up and the moment passed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，徐湛之上表告狀，於是悉出檄書選事及同惡人名手跡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xu Zhanzhi submitted a memorial reporting the case; then all the proclamations, selections, and the handwriting of co-conspirators were produced.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xu Zhanzhi reported the plot. Proclamations, appointments, and conspirators' handwriting were all produced.

sentences.zh: 詔收綜等，並皆款服，唯曄不首。

translations.literal: An edict arrested Zong and the others; all confessed fully—only Ye would not confess first.
translations.idiomatic: An edict arrested Zong and the others. All confessed—only Ye would not confess first.

sentences.zh: 上頻使窮詰，乃曰：「熙先苟誣引臣。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly sent men to press the inquiry; he then said, "Xixian falsely implicated your servant."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed the inquiry repeatedly. Ye then said, "Xixian falsely implicated me."

sentences.zh: 」熙先聞曄不服，笑謂殿中將軍沈邵之曰：「凡諸處分、符檄書疏，皆曄所造及改定，云何方作此抵。

translations.literal: " Xixian, hearing Ye would not confess, laughed and told the Palace General Shen Shaozhi, "All orders, talismans, proclamations, and letters were made and revised by Ye—how can he deny this?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xixian, hearing Ye would not confess, laughed and told Shen Shaozhi, "Every order, proclamation, and letter was written and revised by Ye—how can he deny it?"

sentences.zh: 」上示以曄墨蹟，曄乃引罪。

translations.literal: " The Emperor showed Ye's own handwriting; Ye then confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor showed Ye's handwriting; Ye confessed.

sentences.zh: 明日送曄付廷尉，入獄，然後知為湛之所發。

translations.literal: The next day Ye was sent to the Minister of Justice and imprisoned; only then did he know Zhanzhi had reported him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ye was sent to the minister of justice. Only then did he learn Zhanzhi had betrayed him.

sentences.zh: 熙先望風吐款，辭氣不撓，上奇其才，使謂曰：「以卿之才而滯於集書省，理應有異志，此乃我負卿也。

translations.literal: Xixian, seeing the wind, confessed fully; his words and spirit did not bend; the Emperor marveled at his talent and sent word, "With your talent stagnating in the Secretariat, it is fitting you should have divergent intent—this is my failing you."
translations.idiomatic: Xixian confessed at once, unbending in spirit. The emperor marveled at his talent and said, "With talent like yours stuck in the secretariat, no wonder you rebelled—I failed you."

sentences.zh: 」熙先於獄中上書陳謝，並陳天文占候，誡上有骨肉相殘之禍，其言深切。

translations.literal: " Xixian in prison submitted a memorial of thanks and also set forth astronomical prognostication, warning the Emperor of the calamity of kin killing kin; his words were very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: " In prison Xixian submitted thanks and astronomical warnings of kin killing kin; his words were fierce.

sentences.zh: 曄後與謝綜等得隔壁，遙問綜曰：「疑誰所告。

translations.literal: Ye later was able to reach Zong and the others through the adjoining wall and asked from afar, "Who do you suspect reported us?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye later reached Zong through the adjoining wall and asked, "Who do you think reported us?"

sentences.zh: 」綜曰：「不知。

translations.literal: " Zong said, "I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: " Zong said, "I don't know."

sentences.zh: 」曄乃稱徐湛之小名曰：「乃是徐僮也。

translations.literal: " Ye then named Xu Zhanzhi's childhood name and said, "It was Xu Tong."
translations.idiomatic: " Ye named Xu Zhanzhi's childhood name: "It was Xu Tong."

sentences.zh: 」在獄為詩曰：「禍福本無兆，性命歸有極，必至定前期，誰能延一息。

translations.literal: " In prison he composed a poem: "Fortune and calamity originally have no sign; life and fate return to their limit. The appointed time must come beforehand—who can extend one breath?
translations.idiomatic: " In prison he wrote: "Fortune and calamity have no sign; life returns to its limit. The appointed hour must come—who can draw one more breath?

sentences.zh: 在生已可知，來緣或無識，好醜共一丘，何足異枉直。

translations.literal: In life it can already be known; coming karma perhaps cannot be known. Beauty and ugliness share one mound—what need to distinguish crooked from straight?
translations.idiomatic: Life can be known; what comes after perhaps cannot. Beauty and ugliness share one mound—why distinguish crooked from straight?

sentences.zh: 豈論東陵上，寧辨首山側，雖無嵇生琴，庶同夏侯色。

translations.literal: Why speak of Dongling above? How distinguish the side of Shoushan? Though there is no Ji Kang's zither, I hope to match Xiahou's countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Why speak of Dongling? Why distinguish Shoushan's side? Though I have no Ji Kang's zither, I hope to match Xiahou's face.

sentences.zh: 寄言生存子，此路行復即。

translations.literal: A word to the living sons: this road will soon be taken again.
translations.idiomatic: Word to the living: this road will soon be taken again.

sentences.zh: 」上有白團扇甚佳，送曄令書出詩賦美句。

translations.literal: " The Emperor had a fine white round fan and sent it to Ye, ordering him to write out fine lines of poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had a fine white round fan and sent it to Ye, ordering fine lines of poetry.

sentences.zh: 曄受旨援筆而書曰：「去白日之照照，襲長夜之悠悠。

translations.literal: Ye received the command, took up the brush and wrote, "Departing the sun's bright shining, entering the long night's lingering gloom."
translations.idiomatic: Ye took up the brush and wrote, "Departing the sun's bright shining, entering the long night's lingering gloom."

sentences.zh: 」上循覽淒然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor read it through and was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read it through, deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 曄本謂入獄便死，而上窮其獄，遂經二旬，曄更有生望。

translations.literal: Ye originally thought that entering prison he would die at once; yet the Emperor pressed the case to the end, and after twenty days Ye again had hope of life.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had thought prison meant instant death; yet the emperor pressed the case for twenty days, and hope returned.

sentences.zh: 獄吏因戲之曰：「外傳詹事或當長系。

translations.literal: The prison clerk therefore joked with him, saying, "Outside it is rumored the grand tutor may be long imprisoned."
translations.idiomatic: The prison clerk joked, "Outside they say the grand tutor may be long imprisoned."

sentences.zh: 」曄聞之驚喜。

translations.literal: " Ye, hearing this, was startled and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Ye was startled—and pleased.

sentences.zh: 綜、熙先笑之曰：「詹事嘗共論事，無不攘袂瞋目，及在西池射堂上，躍馬顧眄，自以為一世之雄，而今擾攘紛紜，畏死乃爾。

translations.literal: Zong and Xixian laughed at him and said, "The grand tutor often discussed affairs with us, never failing to roll up his sleeves and glare; yet at the western pool archery hall he leaped on a horse and looked back, thinking himself a hero of the age—and now in turmoil and confusion he fears death thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zong and Xixian laughed: "The grand tutor always rolled up his sleeves and glared when we debated—yet at the archery hall he leaped on a horse, thinking himself a hero of the age. Now he fears death like this."

sentences.zh: 設令今時賜以性命，人臣圖主，何顏可以生存。

translations.literal: Suppose now life were granted—what face could a minister who plotted against his lord use to live?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose life were granted now—what face could a traitor use to live?

sentences.zh: 」曄謂衛獄將曰：「惜哉，埋如此人。

translations.literal: " Ye told the prison guard, "Pity—burying such a man."
translations.idiomatic: " Ye told the guard, "Pity—to bury such a man."

sentences.zh: 」將曰：「不忠之人，亦何足惜。

translations.literal: " The guard said, "An unfaithful man—what is there to pity?"
translations.idiomatic: " The guard said, "A traitor—what is there to pity?"

sentences.zh: 」曄曰：「大將言是也。

translations.literal: " Ye said, "The grand tutor speaks rightly."
translations.idiomatic: " Ye said, "The grand tutor speaks rightly."

sentences.zh: 」及將詣市，曄最在前，于獄門顧謂綜曰：「次第當以位邪？

translations.literal: " When they were to go to the market, Ye was foremost; at the prison gate he looked back and asked Zong, "Should order follow rank?"
translations.idiomatic: " Going to the market, Ye was first. At the prison gate he asked Zong, "Should order follow rank?"

sentences.zh: 」綜曰：「賊帥當為先。

translations.literal: " Zong said, "The rebel chief should go first."
translations.idiomatic: " Zong said, "The rebel chief goes first."

sentences.zh: 」在道語笑，初無慚恥。

translations.literal: On the road they talked and laughed, at first without shame.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they talked and laughed without shame.

sentences.zh: 至市問綜曰：「時欲至未？

translations.literal: Reaching the market he asked Zong, "Has the time nearly come?"
translations.idiomatic: At the market he asked Zong, "Is the time nearly come?"

sentences.zh: 」綜曰：「勢不復久。

translations.literal: " Zong said, "It cannot last much longer."
translations.idiomatic: " Zong said, "Not much longer."

sentences.zh: 」曄既食，又苦勸綜，綜曰：「此異疾篤，何事強飯。

translations.literal: " After Ye had eaten, he again strongly urged Zong to eat; Zong said, "This is a different severe illness—why force food?"
translations.idiomatic: " After eating, Ye urged Zong to eat. Zong said, "This is a different sickness—why force food?"

sentences.zh: 」曄家人悉至市，監刑職司問曰：「須相見不？

translations.literal: " Ye's household all reached the market; the execution officer asked, "Do you wish to meet them?"
translations.idiomatic: " Ye's household arrived. The execution officer asked, "Do you wish to see them?"

sentences.zh: 」曄問綜曰：「家人已來，幸得相見，將不暫別？

translations.literal: " Ye asked Zong, "The household has come—we may meet; will it not be a brief parting?"
translations.idiomatic: " Ye asked Zong, "They've come—we can meet. Won't parting be brief?"

sentences.zh: 」綜曰：「別與不別，亦何所存，來必當號泣，正足亂人意。

translations.literal: " Zong said, "Parting or not—what is there to keep? If they come they will surely wail and only disturb the mind."
translations.idiomatic: " Zong said, "Parting or not—what difference? They'll wail and only disturb us."

sentences.zh: 」曄曰：「號泣何關人，向見道邊親故相瞻望，吾意故欲相見。

translations.literal: " Ye said, "Wailing—what has it to do with others? I saw kinsmen and old friends gazing from the roadside; my heart indeed wished to meet."
translations.idiomatic: " Ye said, "Wailing concerns others how? I saw kinsmen gazing from the road—I wanted to meet them."

sentences.zh: 」於是呼前。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he called them forward.
translations.idiomatic: " He called them forward.

sentences.zh: 曄妻先撫其子，回罵曄曰：「君不為百歲阿家，不感天子恩遇，身死固不足塞罪，奈何枉殺子孫。

translations.literal: Ye's wife first stroked their son, then turned and reviled Ye, saying, "You would not think of your aged mother for a hundred years, nor feel the Emperor's gracious treatment—your death indeed cannot repay guilt, yet why wrongly kill sons and grandsons?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye's wife stroked their son, then reviled Ye: "You won't think of your aged mother, won't feel the emperor's grace—your death can't repay guilt, yet why kill our sons and grandsons?"

sentences.zh: 」曄乾笑，雲罪至而已。

translations.literal: " Ye gave a dry laugh and said guilt had reached its limit—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: " Ye gave a dry laugh: guilt had reached its limit, that was all.

sentences.zh: 曄所生母對泣曰：「主上念汝無極，汝曾不能感恩，又不念我老，今日奈何！

translations.literal: Ye's birth mother wept facing him and said, "The sovereign thought of you beyond measure; you could not repay grace, nor think of my old age—what now!"
translations.idiomatic: His birth mother wept: "The sovereign favored you beyond measure; you repaid no grace, thought not of my old age—what now!"

sentences.zh: 」仍以手擊曄頸及頰。

translations.literal: " She then struck Ye's neck and cheeks with her hand.
translations.idiomatic: " She struck his neck and cheeks.

sentences.zh: 曄妻云：「罪人，阿家莫憶莫念。

translations.literal: Ye's wife said, "Criminal—Mother, do not remember, do not think."
translations.idiomatic: Ye's wife said, "Criminal—Mother, forget him."

sentences.zh: 」妹及妓妾來別，曄乃悲泣流漣。

translations.literal: " His younger sister and singing girls and concubines came to part; Ye then wept with flowing tears.
translations.idiomatic: His sister, singing girls, and concubines came to part; Ye wept.

sentences.zh: 綜曰：「舅殊不及夏侯色。

translations.literal: " Zong said, "Uncle falls far short of Xiahou's countenance."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said, "Uncle falls far short of Xiahou's face."

sentences.zh: 」曄收淚而已。

translations.literal: " Ye wiped his tears and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: " Ye wiped his tears and stopped.

sentences.zh: 綜母以子弟自陷逆亂，獨不出視。

translations.literal: Zong's mother, because her sons and younger brothers had fallen into treason, alone did not come out to look.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's mother, whose sons had fallen into treason, would not come out to look.

sentences.zh: 曄語綜曰：「姊今不來，勝人多也。

translations.literal: Ye told Zong, "Your elder sister not coming today surpasses many people."
translations.idiomatic: Ye told Zong, "Your sister not coming today surpasses many."

sentences.zh: 」曄轉醉，子藹亦醉，取地土及果皮以擲曄，呼為別駕數十聲。

translations.literal: " Ye turned drunk; his son Ai also drunk, took earth and fruit peels and threw them at Ye, calling him Vice Director dozens of times.
translations.idiomatic: Ye grew drunk; his son Ai, also drunk, threw dirt and fruit peels at him, calling him Vice Director dozens of times.

sentences.zh: 曄問曰：「汝瞋我邪？

translations.literal: " Ye asked, "Are you angry at me?"
translations.idiomatic: " Ye asked, "Are you angry at me?"

sentences.zh: 」藹曰：「今日何緣復瞋，但父子同死，不能不悲耳。」

translations.literal: " Ai said, "Why be angry today? Only that father and son die together—I cannot but grieve."
translations.idiomatic: " Ai said, "Why angry today? Father and son die together—I cannot but grieve."

sentences.zh: 曄性精微，有思致，觸類多善，衣裳器服，莫不增損制度，世人皆法學之。

translations.literal: Ye's nature was subtle and refined, with thoughtful invention; in every category he was often good; clothes and vessels—none he did not adjust and set in regulation, and people of the age all studied and copied him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's nature was subtle and refined, inventive in every category. Clothes and vessels—none he did not redesign, and the age copied him.

sentences.zh: 撰和香方，其序之曰：「麝本多忌，過分必害。

translations.literal: He compiled a Formula for Blending Incense, prefacing it: "Musk by nature has many taboos; excess must harm.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a Formula for Blending Incense, prefacing it: "Musk has many taboos; excess harms.

sentences.zh: 沈實易和，盈斤無傷。

translations.literal: Agarwood is solid and easy to blend; a full pound does no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Agarwood is solid and blends easily; a full pound does no harm.

sentences.zh: 零藿虛燥，詹唐黏濕。

translations.literal: Linghuo is empty and dry; zhantang is sticky and damp.
translations.idiomatic: Linghuo is hollow and dry; zhantang is sticky and damp.

sentences.zh: 甘松、蘇合、安息、郁金、奈多、和羅之屬，並被珍於外國，無取於中土。

translations.literal: Gansong, suhe, anxi, yujin, naiduo, heluo and the like are all prized in foreign lands and have no use in the central land.
translations.idiomatic: Gansong, suhe, anxi, yujin, naiduo, heluo and the like are prized abroad and useless in the central lands.

sentences.zh: 又棗膏昏鈍，甲煎淺俗，非唯無助於馨烈，乃當彌增于尤疾也。

translations.literal: Again, jujube paste is dull and obtuse, and armor-boiled extract is shallow and vulgar—they not only do not aid fragrance and strength but will only increase serious faults.
translations.idiomatic: Jujube paste is dull; armor-boiled extract is vulgar—they not only fail fragrance but add serious faults.

sentences.zh: 」所言悉以比類朝士：麝本多忌，比庾仲文；

translations.literal: " All he said was by analogy to court gentlemen: musk's many taboos compared to Yu Zhongwen;
translations.idiomatic: " All was analogy to court gentlemen: musk's taboos compared to Yu Zhongwen;

sentences.zh: 零藿虛燥，比何尚之；

translations.literal: linghuo empty and dry compared to He Shangzhi;
translations.idiomatic: linghuo empty and dry to He Shangzhi;

sentences.zh: 詹唐黏濕，比沈演之；

translations.literal: zhantang sticky and damp compared to Shen Yanzhi;
translations.idiomatic: zhantang sticky and damp to Shen Yanzhi;

sentences.zh: 棗膏昏鈍，比羊玄保；

translations.literal: jujube paste dull and obtuse compared to Yang Xuanbao;
translations.idiomatic: jujube paste dull to Yang Xuanbao;

sentences.zh: 甲煎淺俗，比徐湛之；

translations.literal: armor-boiled extract shallow and vulgar compared to Xu Zhanzhi;
translations.idiomatic: armor-boiled extract vulgar to Xu Zhanzhi;

sentences.zh: 甘松蘇合，比慧琳道人；

translations.literal: gansong and suhe compared to the monk Huilin;
translations.idiomatic: gansong and suhe to the monk Huilin;

sentences.zh: 沈實易和，以自比也。

translations.literal: agarwood solid and easy to blend—he compared himself.
translations.idiomatic: agarwood solid and easy to blend—himself.

sentences.zh: 曄獄中與諸生侄書以自序，其略曰：

translations.literal: In prison Ye wrote to his nephews and students a self-account; the outline says:
translations.idiomatic: In prison Ye wrote a self-account to his nephews; in outline:

sentences.zh: 吾少懶學問，年三十許，始有尚耳。

translations.literal: I was lazy in learning when young; only around thirty did I first have aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: I was lazy in youth; only around thirty did aspiration come.

sentences.zh: 自爾以來，轉為心化，至於所通處，皆自得之胸懷。

translations.literal: From then on my heart transformed; in whatever I penetrated, all came from my own breast.
translations.idiomatic: From then my heart transformed; whatever I mastered came from my own breast.

sentences.zh: 常謂情志所托，故當以意為主，以文傳意。

translations.literal: I always said that what feeling and intent rely on should take intent as master and transmit intent through writing.
translations.idiomatic: I always held that feeling and intent should take intent as master and transmit intent through writing.

sentences.zh: 以意為主，則其旨必見；

translations.literal: Taking intent as master, then its aim must appear;
translations.idiomatic: Take intent as master, and the aim appears;

sentences.zh: 以文傳意，則其辭不流。

translations.literal: transmitting intent through writing, then its words do not flow away.
translations.idiomatic: transmit through writing, and words do not flow away.

sentences.zh: 然後抽其芬芳，振其金石耳。

translations.literal: Then one may draw out fragrance and strike metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Then one draws out fragrance and strikes metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 觀古今文人多不全了此處，年少中謝莊最有其分，手筆差易，于文不拘韻故也。

translations.literal: Looking at writers ancient and modern, many do not fully understand this place; among the young Xie Zhuang had most of this quality—his hand flowed easily, and in writing he was not bound by rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Most writers ancient and modern miss this; among the young Xie Zhuang had most of it—his hand flowed easily, unbound by rhyme.

sentences.zh: 吾思乃無定方，但多公家之言，少於事外遠致，以此為恨，亦由無意于文名故也。

translations.literal: My thought has no fixed direction, but mostly public words; less of matters outside and far-reaching intent—this I regret, also because I had no mind for literary fame.
translations.idiomatic: My thought has no fixed direction—mostly official words, less of distant intent. I regret this, having no mind for literary fame.

sentences.zh: 本未開史書，政恒覺其不可解耳。

translations.literal: Originally I had not opened historical writing; I always felt it could not be understood.
translations.idiomatic: I had not opened historical writing; I always felt it could not be understood.

sentences.zh: 既造後漢，轉得統緒。

translations.literal: Having made the Later Han, I then obtained the thread.
translations.idiomatic: Making the Later Han, I then found the thread.

sentences.zh: 詳觀古今著述及評論，殆少可意者。

translations.literal: Looking carefully at writings and commentaries ancient and modern, scarcely any fully satisfy.
translations.idiomatic: Looking carefully at writings and commentaries ancient and modern, scarcely any satisfy.

sentences.zh: 班氏最有高名，既任情無例，唯志可推耳。

translations.literal: The Ban clan has the highest name; they indulged feeling without rule—only the Treatises can be pushed forward.
translations.idiomatic: The Ban clan has the highest name; they indulged feeling without rule—only the Treatises stand.

sentences.zh: 博贍不可及之，整理未必愧也。

translations.literal: In broad learning they cannot be reached; in ordering they may not be ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: In breadth they cannot be reached; in ordering I may not be ashamed.

sentences.zh: 吾雜傳論皆有精意深旨，至於循吏以下及六夷諸序論，筆勢縱放，實天下之奇作。

translations.literal: My assorted biography commentaries all have refined intent and deep aim; as for the orderly officials below and the six barbarian preface commentaries, the brush momentum is unrestrained—they are truly marvels under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: My biography commentaries have refined intent; the orderly officials and six barbarian prefaces are unrestrained—truly marvels under heaven.

sentences.zh: 其中合者，往往不減過秦篇。

translations.literal: Among them what fits often does not fall short of the "Discourse on Qin."
translations.idiomatic: What fits often does not fall short of the "Discourse on Qin."

sentences.zh: 嘗共比方班氏所作，非但不愧之而已。

translations.literal: I once compared them with the Ban clan's work—not only without shame but more.
translations.idiomatic: I compared them with the Ban clan—not only without shame but more.

sentences.zh: 欲遍作諸志，前漢所有者悉令備，雖事不必多，且使見文得盡。

translations.literal: I wished to make all the Treatises completely, all that the Former Han had to be supplied; though affairs need not be many, let the writing be fully seen.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to make all Treatises the Former Han had, complete; affairs need not be many, but writing should be full.

sentences.zh: 又欲因事就卷內發論，以正一代得失，意復不果。

translations.literal: Again I wished to raise commentaries within the scrolls on affairs, to correct a generation's gains and losses—intent again did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to raise commentaries within the scrolls to correct a generation's gains and losses—intent again failed.

sentences.zh: 贊自是吾文傑思，殆無一字空設，奇變不窮，同合異體，乃自不知所以稱之。

translations.literal: The Eulogies are truly my literary masterpiece; scarcely one word is empty; strange changes without end, same in joining yet different in form—I myself do not know how to name them.
translations.idiomatic: The Eulogies are my masterpiece; scarcely one word empty; strange changes without end—I myself do not know how to name them.

sentences.zh: 此書行，故應有賞音者。

translations.literal: When this book circulates, there should be those who appreciate its tone.
translations.idiomatic: When this book circulates, there should be those who appreciate its tone.

sentences.zh: 紀傳例為舉其大略耳，諸細意甚多。

translations.literal: The annal-biography examples give the great outline; the fine points are very many.
translations.idiomatic: The annal-biography examples give the outline; fine points are many.

sentences.zh: 自古體大而思精，未有此也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity none has been so large in body and so refined in thought.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity none so large in body and refined in thought.

sentences.zh: 恐世人不能盡之，多貴古賤今，所以稱情狂言耳。

translations.literal: I fear people of the world cannot fully understand; many prize the old and despise the present—therefore I speak feeling in wild words.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the world cannot fully understand; many prize the old and despise the present—therefore wild words.

sentences.zh: 吾於音樂，聽功不及自揮，但所精非雅聲為可恨，然至於一絕處，亦復何異邪。

translations.literal: In music my hearing in performance does not match my playing; what I refined was not elegant sound—this is regrettable; yet at the one supreme place, what difference is there?
translations.idiomatic: In music my ear falls short of my hand; what I refined was not elegant sound—regrettable; yet at the supreme place, what difference?

sentences.zh: 其中體趣，言之不可盡。

translations.literal: The inner tone within—words cannot exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: The inner tone—words cannot exhaust it.

sentences.zh: 弦外之意，虛響之音，不知所從而來。

translations.literal: Intent beyond the strings, empty resonance of sound—I do not know whence it comes.
translations.idiomatic: Intent beyond the strings, empty resonance—I do not know whence it comes.

sentences.zh: 亦嘗以授人，士庶中未有一毫似者，此永不傳矣。

translations.literal: I also once taught others; among commoners and officials not one was the least like it—this will never be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: I taught others; among commoners and officials not one was the least like it—this will never transmit.

sentences.zh: 吾書雖小小有意，筆勢不快，餘竟不成就，每愧此名。

translations.literal: My writing though small has some intent; brush momentum is not swift—yet in the end not accomplished; I always regret this name.
translations.idiomatic: My writing has small intent; brush is not swift—yet never accomplished; I regret the name.

sentences.zh: 曄自序並實，故存之。

translations.literal: Ye's self-account is true and therefore preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's self-account is true and therefore preserved.

sentences.zh: 藹幼而整潔，衣服竟歲未嘗有塵點，死時年二十。

translations.literal: Ai from youth was neat; his clothes for a whole year never had a speck of dust; he died at twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Ai from youth was neat; his clothes a whole year without a speck of dust; he died at twenty.

sentences.zh: 曄少時，兄晏常云：「此兒進利，終破門戶。

translations.literal: When Ye was young his elder brother Yan often said, "This boy advances for profit and will in the end ruin the house."
translations.idiomatic: When Ye was young his brother Yan said, "This boy advances for profit and will ruin the house."

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: " It indeed happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: " It happened as he said.

sentences.zh: 初，何尚之處銓衡，自謂天下無滯才，及熙先就拘，帝詰尚之曰：「使孔熙先年三十猶作散騎侍郎，那不作賊。

translations.literal: Earlier, when He Shangzhi held the balance of selection, he claimed that under heaven there was no stalled talent; when Xixian was taken in custody, the Emperor questioned Shangzhi, saying, "If Kong Xixian at thirty were still Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant, would he not become a rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: When He Shangzhi held selection, he claimed no talent stalled under heaven. When Xixian was taken, the emperor asked, "If Kong Xixian at thirty were still supernumerary cavalry attendant, would he not rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」熙先死後，又謂尚之曰：「孔熙先有美才，地胄猶可論，而翳跡仕流，豈非時匠失乎？

translations.literal: " After Xixian died, he again told Shangzhi, "Kong Xixian had fine talent; his gate and ancestry could still be discussed, yet he hid his traces in the official stream—is this not the age's craftsman failing?"
translations.idiomatic: " After Xixian died he told Shangzhi, "Kong Xixian had fine talent and decent ancestry, yet hid in the official stream—is the age's craftsman failing?"

sentences.zh: 」尚之曰：「臣昔謬得待罪選曹，誠無以濯汙揚清；

translations.literal: " Shangzhi said, "Your servant formerly wrongly received blame in the Selection Bureau and truly had no means to wash the foul and raise the clear;
translations.idiomatic: " Shangzhi said, "I wrongly served selection and truly could not wash the foul and raise the clear;

sentences.zh: 然君子之有智慧，猶鵷鳳之有文采，俟時而振羽翼，何患不出雲霞之上。

translations.literal: yet when a gentleman has wisdom, it is like the luan and phoenix having pattern—wait for the time and beat the wings; what fear of not rising above cloud and haze?
translations.idiomatic: yet when a gentleman has wisdom, like luan and phoenix having pattern—wait for the time and beat wings; what fear of not rising above the clouds?

sentences.zh: 若熙先必蘊文采，自棄於污泥，終無論矣。

translations.literal: If Xixian truly harbored literary pattern and cast himself into mud, in the end there is nothing to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: If Xixian truly had literary gifts and cast himself into mud, there is nothing to discuss.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「昔有良才而不遇知己者，何嘗不遺恨於後哉。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "In old times there were fine talents who did not meet knowing lords—how could they not leave regret for later?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Fine talents who missed knowing lords—how could they not leave regret?"

sentences.zh: 荀伯子，潁川潁陰人，晉驃騎將軍羨之孫也。

translations.literal: Xun Bozi was a man of Yingyin in Yingchuan, grandson of the Jin Cavalry General-in-Chief Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Bozi was from Yingyin in Yingchuan, grandson of the Jin cavalry general-in-chief Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 父猗，秘書郎。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 伯子少好學，博覽經傳，而通率好為雜語，遨遊閭里，故以此失清途。

translations.literal: Bozi from youth loved learning, read widely in classics and transmissions, yet was open and free and loved to make miscellaneous talk, roaming lanes and villages—therefore he lost the clear path on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Bozi from youth loved learning and read widely, yet was open and free, loved gossip, and roamed the lanes—therefore he lost the clear path.

sentences.zh: 解褐駙馬都尉、奉朝請、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: On leaving the robe he became Commandant of the Horse Guard, Attendant at the Morning Audience, and Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving the robe he became commandant of the horse guard, attendant at morning audience, and supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 著作郎徐廣重其才學，舉伯子及王韶之並為佐郎，同撰晉史及著桓玄等傳。

translations.literal: The Compiler Xu Guang valued his talent and learning and recommended Bozi together with Wang Shaozhi as assistant compilers, jointly compiling the Jin History and composing biographies of Huan Xuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang valued his talent and recommended Bozi with Wang Shaozhi as assistant compilers, jointly compiling the Jin History and biographies of Huan Xuan and others.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to senior clerk of the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年，上表稱：「故太傅钜平侯羊祜勳參佐命，功盛平吳，而享嗣闕然，蒸嘗莫寄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi he submitted a memorial saying, "The former Grand Tutor Marquis of Juping Yang Hu assisted in the mandate, his merit surpassing the pacification of Wu, yet sacrifices to descendants are lacking and offerings have no resting place.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 1 he submitted a memorial: "Former Grand Tutor Marquis of Juping Yang Hu assisted the mandate, his merit surpassing the pacification of Wu, yet sacrifices to descendants are lacking.

sentences.zh: 漢以蕭何元功，故絕世輒紹，愚謂钜平之封，宜同酇國。

translations.literal: Han because of Xiao He's primal merit, when the line ended always continued the succession—I foolishly think the enfeoffment of Juping should be like the state of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Han because of Xiao He's primal merit continued the line when it ended—I think Juping's enfeoffment should be like Zan.

sentences.zh: 故太尉廣陵公陳准党翼孫秀，禍加淮南，竊饗大國，因罪為利。

translations.literal: The former Grand Commandant Marquis of Guangling Chen Huai sided with Sun Xiu, disaster reaching Huainan, yet secretly enjoyed a great state and turned crime into profit.
translations.idiomatic: Former Grand Commandant Marquis of Guangling Chen Huai sided with Sun Xiu, disaster reaching Huainan, yet enjoyed a great state and turned crime to profit.

sentences.zh: 會西朝政刑失裁，中興復因而不奪，今王道惟新，豈可不大判臧否？

translations.literal: When the Western Court lost measure in punishment, the Restoration again followed and did not revoke; now the kingly way is newly renewed—how can one not greatly judge good and evil?
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Court lost measure in punishment, the Restoration followed and did not revoke. Now the kingly way is renewed—how not judge good and evil?
