sentences.zh: 謂廣陵之國，宜在削除。

translations.literal: I say the state of Guangling should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling's state should be removed.

sentences.zh: 故太保衛瓘本爵菑陽縣公，既被橫禍，乃進第秩，加贈蘭陵，又轉江夏。

translations.literal: The former Grand Protector Wei Guan's original enfeoffment was Marquis of Ziyang County; having suffered violent calamity, his rank was then advanced, additionally enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, and again transferred to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Former Grand Protector Wei Guan's original enfeoffment was marquis of Ziyang county; suffering violent calamity, rank advanced, additionally duke of Lanling, then Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 中朝公輔，多非理終，瓘功德不殊，亦無緣獨受偏賞。

translations.literal: Middle-court public assistants mostly did not end by reason; Guan's merit and virtue were not different—there was also no reason he alone should receive partial reward.
translations.idiomatic: Middle-court ministers mostly did not end by reason; Guan's merit was not different—no reason for partial reward.

sentences.zh: 宜復本封，以正國章。

translations.literal: He should restore the original enfeoffment to correct the state's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the original enfeoffment to correct state regulations.

sentences.zh: 」詔付門下。

translations.literal: " An edict was sent to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict went to the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 前散騎常侍江夏公衛璵及潁川陳茂先各自陳先代勳，不伏貶降。

translations.literal: The former Supernumerary Regular Attendant Duke of Jiangxia Wei Jun and Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan each stated their ancestors' merit and would not submit to demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Former supernumerary attendant Duke of Jiangxia Wei Jun and Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan each stated ancestral merit and would not submit to demotion.

sentences.zh: 詔皆付門下，並不施行。

translations.literal: Edicts all went to the Secretariat and were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts went to the secretariat and were not carried out.

sentences.zh: 伯子為妻弟謝晦薦達，為尚書左丞，出補臨川內史。

translations.literal: Bozi recommended his wife's younger brother Xie Hui for advancement and became Senior Clerk of the Ministry of the Interior, then went out to supplement Internal Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bozi recommended his brother-in-law Xie Hui and became senior clerk of the interior, then internal administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍王弘稱伯子「沈重不華，有平陽侯之風」。

translations.literal: The General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Hong called Bozi "weighty without display, having the air of Marquis of Pingyang."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, general of chariots and cavalry, called Bozi "weighty without display, with the air of the Marquis of Pingyang."

sentences.zh: 伯子常自矜藉蔭之美，謂弘曰：「天下膏粱，唯使君與下官耳，宣明之徒不足數也。

translations.literal: Bozi often prided himself on the beauty of inherited shade and told Hong, "Under heaven only Your Grace and your servant—men like Xuanming are not worth counting."
translations.idiomatic: Bozi often prided himself on inherited privilege and told Hong, "Under heaven only you and I—men like Xuanming aren't worth counting."

sentences.zh: 」遷散騎常侍，又上表曰：「百官位次，陳留王在零陵王上，臣愚竊以為疑。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant and again submitted a memorial saying, "In the ranking of the hundred offices, the Prince of Chenliu stands above the Prince of Lingling—I your servant foolishly think this doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made supernumerary regular attendant and submitted another memorial: "In ranking the hundred offices, the Prince of Chenliu stands above the Prince of Lingling—I think this doubtful.

sentences.zh: 昔武王克殷，封神農後於焦，黃帝后于祝，帝堯後於薊，帝舜後於陳，夏後後於杞，殷後於宋。

translations.literal: When King Wu conquered Yin he enfeoffed Shen Nong's descendant at Jiao, Huang Di's at Zhu, Emperor Yao's at Ji, Emperor Shun's at Chen, the Xia descendant at Qi, and the Yin at Song.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu conquered Yin he enfeoffed Shen Nong's descendant at Jiao, Huang Di's at Zhu, Yao's at Ji, Shun's at Chen, Xia at Qi, Yin at Song.

sentences.zh: 杞、陳並為列國，而薊、祝、焦無聞。

translations.literal: Qi and Chen both became feudal states, while Ji, Zhu, and Jiao are unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Chen became feudal states; Ji, Zhu, and Jiao are unheard of.

sentences.zh: 斯則褒崇所承，優於遠代之顯驗也。

translations.literal: This then is that what honor and exaltation inherit is superior to the visible proof of distant ages.
translations.idiomatic: What honor inherits is superior to distant ages' visible proof.

sentences.zh: 是以春秋次序諸侯，宋居杞、陳之上，考之近代，事亦有征。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Spring and Autumn Annals the order of feudal lords places Song above Qi and Chen—examining recent ages, affairs also have proof.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals places Song above Qi and Chen—recent ages too have proof.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始元年，詔賜山陽公劉康子弟一人爵關內侯，衛公姬署、宋侯孔紹子弟一人駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi of Jin, an edict granted Liu Kang, Duke of Shanyang, one man of his clan the rank of Marquis Within the Passes; Ji Shu, Duke of Wei, and Kong Shao, Marquis of Song, one man each as Commandant of the Horse Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taishi 1 granted Liu Kang, duke of Shanyang, one clansman rank of marquis within the passes; Ji Shu, duke of Wei, and Kong Shao, marquis of Song, one each as commandant of the horse guard.

sentences.zh: 又泰始三年，太常上言博士劉嘉等議，稱衛公署于大晉在三恪之數，應降稱侯。

translations.literal: Again in the third year of Taishi the Minister of Ceremonies submitted that the Erudite Liu Jia and others debated, saying Duke Wei Shu in great Jin was in the number of the Three Honored and should be demoted to be called marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 3 the minister of ceremonies submitted that Erudite Liu Jia debated Duke Wei Shu in great Jin was among the Three Honored and should be demoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 臣以為零陵王位宜在陳留之上。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks the Prince of Lingling's rank should stand above Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lingling's rank should stand above Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " It was followed.

sentences.zh: 為御史中丞，蒞職勤恪，有匪躬之稱。

translations.literal: He became Censor-in-Chief; in office he was diligent and had the name of not sparing himself.
translations.idiomatic: He became censor-in-chief, diligent in office, not sparing himself.

sentences.zh: 立朝正色，眾咸憚之。

translations.literal: Standing at court with upright countenance, the multitude all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Standing at court with upright countenance, all feared him.

sentences.zh: 凡所奏劾，莫不深相訶毀，或延及祖禰，示其切直。

translations.literal: Whatever he impeached, none he did not deeply revile; sometimes it extended to ancestors and fathers, showing his cutting directness.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he impeached he reviled deeply, sometimes reaching ancestors, showing cutting directness.

sentences.zh: 又頗雜嘲戲，故世人以此非之。

translations.literal: Again he often mixed in mockery and jest; therefore people of the world on this account criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: He often mixed mockery and jest; the world criticized him for it.

sentences.zh: 補司徒左長史，卒于東陽太守。

translations.literal: He supplemented Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and died as Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became left chief clerk of the minister of works and died as governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 文集傳於世。

translations.literal: A collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collected works circulated.

sentences.zh: 子赤松，為尚書右丞，以徐湛之党，為元凶所殺。

translations.literal: His son Chisong was Senior Clerk of the Ministry of the Interior on the right and was killed by the Crown Prince as a partisan of Xu Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chisong was senior clerk of the interior on the right and was killed by the crown prince as Xu Zhanzhi's partisan.

sentences.zh: 伯子族弟昶字茂祖，與伯子絕服，元嘉初，以文義至中書郎。

translations.literal: Bozi's clansman younger brother Chang, styled Maozu, ended mourning with Bozi; at the beginning of Yuanjia, through literary meaning he reached Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Bozi's clansman Chang, styled Maozu, ended mourning with Bozi; at Yuanjia's start, through literary gifts he reached secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 昶子萬秋。

translations.literal: Chang's son Wanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's son Wanqiu.

sentences.zh: 萬秋字元寶，亦用才學自顯。

translations.literal: Wanqiu, styled Yuanbao, also by talent and learning made himself visible.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqiu, styled Yuanbao, also made himself visible by talent.

sentences.zh: 昶見釋慧琳，謂曰：「昨萬秋對策，欲以相示。

translations.literal: Chang saw the monk Huilin and said, "Yesterday Wanqiu answered at examination—I wish to show it to you."
translations.idiomatic: Chang saw the monk Huilin and said, "Yesterday Wanqiu answered at examination—I wish to show you."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「此不須看。

translations.literal: " He answered, "This need not be seen.
translations.idiomatic: " Huilin answered, "No need to see it.

sentences.zh: 若非先見而答，貧道不能為；

translations.literal: If not answering after prior sight, this poor monk cannot do it;
translations.idiomatic: If not answering after prior sight, I cannot do it;

sentences.zh: 若先見而答，貧道奴皆能為。

translations.literal: if answering after prior sight, this poor monk's slaves can all do it.
translations.idiomatic: if answering after prior sight, my slaves can all do it.

sentences.zh: 」昶曰：「此將不傷道德耶？

translations.literal: " Chang said, "Will this not harm virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "Does this not harm virtue?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「大德所以不德。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Great virtue therefore is not virtuous."
translations.idiomatic: " Huilin answered, "Great virtue therefore is not virtuous."

sentences.zh: 」乃相對笑，竟不看焉。

translations.literal: " They then laughed facing each other and in the end did not look.
translations.idiomatic: " They laughed and never looked.

sentences.zh: 萬秋孝武初為晉陵太守，坐于郡立華林合，置主衣、主書，下獄免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaowu, Wanqiu was Administrator of Jinling; for establishing the Hualin Pavilion in the commandery he was imprisoned and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's start Wanqiu was governor of Jinling; for building the Hualin Pavilion in the commandery he was imprisoned and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝末，為御史中丞，卒官。

translations.literal: At the end of the Deposed Emperor he was Censor-in-Chief and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the deposed emperor's end he was censor-in-chief and died in office.

sentences.zh: 徐廣字野人，東莞姑幕人也。

translations.literal: Xu Guang, styled Yerén, was a man of Gumu in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang, styled Yerén, was from Gumu in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 父藻，都水使者。

translations.literal: His father Zao was Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao was commissioner of waterways.

sentences.zh: 兄邈，太子前衛率。

translations.literal: His elder brother Miao was Forward Commander of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Miao was forward commander of the heir apparent's guard.

sentences.zh: 家世好學，至廣尤精。

translations.literal: The family for generations loved learning; in Guang it was especially refined.
translations.idiomatic: The family for generations loved learning; in Guang it was especially refined.

sentences.zh: 百家數術，無不研覽。

translations.literal: The hundred schools and numerical arts—none he did not study and examine.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred schools and numerical arts—none he did not study.

sentences.zh: 家貧，未嘗以產業為意，妻中山劉謐之女忿之，數以相讓，廣終不改。

translations.literal: The household was poor and he never took property as concern; his wife, daughter of Liu Mi of Zhongshan, resented this and repeatedly reproached him—Guang in the end did not change.
translations.idiomatic: The household was poor and he never cared for property; his wife, Liu Mi's daughter of Zhongshan, resented this and reproached him repeatedly—Guang never changed.

sentences.zh: 如此十數年，家道日弊，遂與廣離。

translations.literal: Thus for more than ten years the household daily declined, and he parted from Guang.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years the household declined daily, and she left him.

sentences.zh: 後晉孝武帝以廣博學，除為秘書郎，校書秘閣，增置職僚。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, because Guang was broadly learned, made him Secretary Gentleman; he collated books in the Secret Repository and additional staff were added.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, finding Guang broadly learned, made him secretariat gentleman; he collated books in the secret repository and staff were added.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，尚書令王珣舉為祠部郎。

translations.literal: In the Long'an era the Minister of the Interior Wang Xun recommended him as Senior Clerk of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an Wang Xun, minister of the interior, recommended him as senior clerk of rites.

sentences.zh: 李太后崩，廣議服曰：「太皇太后名位既正，體同皇極，理製備盡，情禮彌申。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Li died, Guang debated mourning garments, saying, "The Grand Empress Dowager's name and rank are already correct, her body the same as the imperial apex; ritual system is fully prepared, feeling and ritual still more extended.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Li died, Guang debated mourning: "The grand empress dowager's name and rank are correct, her body the same as the imperial apex; ritual is fully prepared, feeling and ritual extended.

sentences.zh: 陽秋之義，母以子貴。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals: the mother is honored through the son.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals: the mother is honored through the son.

sentences.zh: 既稱夫人，禮服從正。

translations.literal: Having called her Lady, mourning garments follow the correct.
translations.idiomatic: Having called her Lady, mourning garments follow the correct form.

sentences.zh: 故成風顯夫人之號，文公服三年之喪，子于父之所生，體尊義重。

translations.literal: Therefore Chengfeng displayed the title of lady; Duke Wen wore three years' mourning; the son for what the father begot—the body is honored and the meaning weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfeng displayed the title of lady; Duke Wen wore three years' mourning; the son for what the father begot—body honored, meaning weighty.

sentences.zh: 且禮祖不厭孫，固宜遂服無屈。

translations.literal: Moreover in ritual the ancestor does not weary of the grandson—it is fitting therefore to follow mourning without bending.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual the ancestor does not weary of the grandson—it is fitting to follow mourning without bending.

sentences.zh: 而緣情立制，若嫌明文不存，則疑斯從重。

translations.literal: Yet establishing system according to feeling—if one suspects the clear text does not exist, then one suspects this follows the heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet establishing system by feeling—if clear text is lacking, follow the heavier rule.

sentences.zh: 謂應同于為祖母後，齊衰三年。

translations.literal: I say it should be the same as for one who succeeds a grandmother—observing mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: It should be the same as succeeding a grandmother—observing mourning three years.

sentences.zh: 」時從其議。

translations.literal: " At the time they followed this debate.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time they followed this debate.

sentences.zh: 及會稽王世子元顯錄尚書，欲使百僚致敬，台內使廣立議，由是內外並執下官禮，廣常為愧恨。

translations.literal: When the Heir of Kuaiji Yuanxian recorded the Ministry of the Interior and wished to make the hundred officials pay homage, the inner office had Guang establish the debate; therefore inside and outside both held the lower-official ritual—Guang was often ashamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuaiji's heir Yuanxian recorded the interior and wished homage from all officials, Guang was made to establish the debate; inside and outside held lower-official ritual—Guang was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，宋武帝使撰車服儀注，仍除鎮軍諮議參軍，領記室，封樂成縣五等侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, Emperor Wu of Song had him compile regulations for carriages, robes, and ritual; he was additionally made Staff Adviser to the General Who Pacifies the Army, concurrently Recorder, and enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Lecheng County.
translations.idiomatic: At Yixi's start Liu Yu had him compile carriage, robe, and ritual regulations; he became staff adviser to the pacifying general, recorder, and fifth-rank marquis of Lecheng county.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎常侍，領著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant and concurrently Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supernumerary cavalry attendant and concurrently compiler.

sentences.zh: 二年，尚書奏廣撰成晉史。

translations.literal: In the second year the Ministry of the Interior submitted that Guang had completed the Jin History.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the interior submitted that Guang had completed the Jin History.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to General of Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made general of rapid cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時有風雹為災，廣獻言武帝，多所勸勉。

translations.literal: At that time wind and hail became disaster; Guang presented words to Emperor Wu with much encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and hail became disaster; Guang presented words to the emperor with much encouragement.

sentences.zh: 又轉大司農，領著作郎，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Again he was transferred to Minister of Public Works, concurrently Compiler, and promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of public works, concurrently compiler, and promoted to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，桓玄篡位，安帝出宮，廣陪列悲慟，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An left the palace, Guang in the ranks grieved and was moved; sorrow moved those left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped and Emperor An left the palace, Guang in the ranks grieved; sorrow moved those beside him.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受禪，恭帝遜位，廣又哀感，涕泗交流。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang again was moved to sorrow and wept with flowing tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu received abdication and Emperor Gong yielded, Guang again wept.

sentences.zh: 謝晦見之，謂曰：「徐公將無小過。

translations.literal: Xie Hui, seeing this, said to him, "Master Xu will perhaps have a small fault."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, seeing this, said, "Master Xu will perhaps have a small fault."

sentences.zh: 」廣收淚答曰：「身與君不同，君佐命興王，逢千載嘉運。

translations.literal: " Guang wiped his tears and answered, "My person and you are not the same—you assisted the mandate and raised the king, meeting a thousand-year auspicious fortune.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang wiped his tears: "You and I are not the same—you assisted the mandate and met a thousand-year fortune.

sentences.zh: 身世荷晉德，眷戀故主。

translations.literal: My person and generation owe Jin virtue and am attached to the former lord."
translations.idiomatic: I owe Jin virtue and am attached to the former lord."

sentences.zh: 」因更歔欷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept again.
translations.idiomatic: He wept again.

sentences.zh: 時有高平郗紹亦作晉中興書，數以示何法盛。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Ping Chi Shao also made the Jin Restoration Book and several times showed it to He Fasheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ping Chi Shao also made the Jin Restoration Book and showed it to He Fasheng.

sentences.zh: 法盛有意圖之，謂紹曰：「卿名位貴達，不復俟此延譽。

translations.literal: Fasheng wished to seize it and told Shao, "Your name and rank are noble and reached—you no longer need this extended fame.
translations.idiomatic: Fasheng wished to seize it and told Shao, "Your rank is noble—you need no extended fame from this.

sentences.zh: 我寒士，無聞于時，如袁宏、干寶之徒，賴有著述，流聲於後。

translations.literal: I am a cold scholar, unknown to the times; men like Yuan Hong and Gan Bao rely on having writings and leave sound for later.
translations.idiomatic: I am a cold scholar, unknown; men like Yuan Hong and Gan Bao rely on writings for later fame.

sentences.zh: 宜以為惠。

translations.literal: You ought to make it a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Make it a gift.

sentences.zh: 」紹不與。

translations.literal: " Shao did not give it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao refused.

sentences.zh: 至書成，在齋內廚中，法盛詣紹，紹不在，直入竊書。

translations.literal: When the book was complete it was in the kitchen of the study; Fasheng went to Shao, Shao was not present, and he entered directly and stole the book.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was complete it was in the study kitchen; Fasheng went, Shao absent, entered and stole it.

sentences.zh: 紹還失之，無復兼本，於是遂行何書。

translations.literal: When Shao returned it was lost and there was no duplicate copy; therefore He's book circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Shao returned to find it gone, no duplicate—He's book circulated.

sentences.zh: 徐豁字萬同，廣兄子也。

translations.literal: Xu Huo, styled Wantong, was Guang's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huo, styled Wantong, was Guang's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父邈，晉太子前衛率。

translations.literal: His father Miao was Forward Commander of the Jin Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Miao was forward commander of the Jin heir's guard.

sentences.zh: 豁宋永初初，為尚書左丞、山陰令，精練法理，為時所推。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu of Song, Huo was Senior Clerk of the Ministry of the Interior on the left and Magistrate of Shanyin; he refined legal principles and was pushed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: At Song Yongchu's start Huo was senior clerk of the interior on the left and magistrate of Shanyin; he refined legal principles and was esteemed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，為始興太守，表陳三事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was Administrator of Shixing and submitted a memorial stating three matters.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanjia's start he was governor of Shixing and submitted three matters.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘉之，賜絹二百匹，穀一千斛。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised it and granted two hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised it and granted two hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 徙廣州刺史，未拜卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Guang Province and died before accepting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Guang Province and died before accepting.

sentences.zh: 鄭鮮之字道子，滎陽開封人，魏將作大匠渾之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xianzhi, styled Daozi, was a man of Kaifeng in Xingyang, great-great-grandson of the Wei Master of Construction Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xianzhi, styled Daozi, was from Kaifeng in Xingyang, great-great-grandson of the Wei master of construction Hun.

sentences.zh: 祖襲，大司農，經為江乘令，因居縣境。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi was Minister of Public Works; having once been Magistrate of Jiangcheng, he therefore dwelt within the county border.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi was minister of public works; once magistrate of Jiangcheng, he dwelt within the county.

sentences.zh: 父遵，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father Zun was Gentleman of the Ministry of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun was a gentleman of the interior.

sentences.zh: 鮮之下帷讀書，絕交遊之務。

translations.literal: Xianzhi lowered the curtain to read books and cut off the business of social intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi lowered the curtain to read and cut off social intercourse.

sentences.zh: 初為桓偉輔國主簿。

translations.literal: At first he was Chief Clerk to Huan Wei, General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was chief clerk to Huan Wei, general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 先是，兗州刺史滕恬為丁零翟遼所沒，屍喪不反。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Inspector of Yan Province Teng Tian was destroyed by the Dingling Zhai Liao; corpse and coffin did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan Province inspector Teng Tian was destroyed by the Dingling Zhai Liao; corpse and coffin never returned.

sentences.zh: 恬子羨仕宦不廢，論者嫌之。

translations.literal: Tian's son Xian served in office without pause; debaters found fault.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's son Xian served on without pause; debaters found fault.

sentences.zh: 桓玄在荊州，使群僚博議。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan was in Jing Province and had the assembled officials broadly debate.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was in Jing Province and had officials broadly debate.

sentences.zh: 鮮之議曰：「名教大極，忠孝而已。

translations.literal: Xianzhi debated, saying, "Name-teaching's great apex is loyalty and filial piety alone.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi debated: "Name-teaching's apex is loyalty and filial piety alone.

sentences.zh: 至乎變通抑引，每事輒殊。

translations.literal: As for change and extension, suppression and citation—each affair is then different.
translations.idiomatic: Change, extension, suppression, citation—each affair differs.

sentences.zh: 本而尋之，皆求心而遺跡。

translations.literal: Tracing to the root and seeking it, all seek the heart and leave the trace.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing to the root, all seek the heart and leave the trace.

sentences.zh: 跡之所乘，遭遇或異。

translations.literal: What the trace rides on—encounter may differ.
translations.idiomatic: What the trace rides on—encounter may differ.

sentences.zh: 故聖人或就跡以助教，或因跡以成罪，屈申與奪，難可等齊，舉其阡陌，皆可終言矣。

translations.literal: Therefore sages sometimes follow the trace to aid teaching, or because of the trace complete guilt; bending and extending, taking and giving, hard to equalize—raising their paths, all can be spoken to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Sages sometimes follow trace to aid teaching, or because of trace complete guilt; bending, extending, taking, giving—hard to equalize.

sentences.zh: 天可逃乎？

translations.literal: Heaven can be fled?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven can be fled?

sentences.zh: 而伊尹廢君；

translations.literal: Yet Yi Yin deposed his lord;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi Yin deposed his lord;

sentences.zh: 君可脅乎？

translations.literal: the lord can be coerced?
translations.idiomatic: the lord can be coerced?

sentences.zh: 而鬻拳見善；

translations.literal: Yet Yuzhan saw good;
translations.idiomatic: yet Yuzhan saw good;

sentences.zh: 忠可愚乎？

translations.literal: loyalty can be foolish?
translations.idiomatic: loyalty can be foolish?

sentences.zh: 而箕子同仁。

translations.literal: Yet Jizi shared the same virtue.
translations.idiomatic: yet Jizi shared the same virtue.

sentences.zh: 自此以還，殊實而齊聲，異譽而等美者，不可勝言。

translations.literal: From this onward, different substance yet same sound, different praise yet equal beauty—cannot be fully spoken.
translations.idiomatic: From this onward, different substance yet same sound, different praise yet equal beauty—countless.

sentences.zh: 今如滕羨情事者，或終身隱處，不關人事，或升朝理務，無譏前哲。

translations.literal: Now as for Teng Xian's situation, some hide all their lives without touching human affairs, or ascend court and manage affairs without reproach from former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: As for Teng Xian's situation, some hide all their lives, or ascend court without reproach from worthies.

sentences.zh: 通滕者則以無譏為證，塞滕者則以隱處為美。

translations.literal: Those who open for Teng take no reproach as proof; those who block Teng take hiding as beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Those who open for Teng take no reproach as proof; those who block take hiding as beauty.

sentences.zh: 折其兩中，則異同之情可見矣。

translations.literal: Breaking the two middles, then the difference and sameness of feeling can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Break the two middles, and feeling's difference and sameness appear.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人立教，猶言有禮無時，君子不行。

translations.literal: Sages establish teaching—still they say there is ritual without timely fit, and the gentleman does not act.
translations.idiomatic: Sages establish teaching—still they say ritual without timely fit, and the gentleman does not act.

sentences.zh: 有禮無時，政以事有變通，不可宗一故耳。」

translations.literal: Ritual without timely fit is because affairs have change and extension and cannot be bound to one alone."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual without timely fit—affairs have change and cannot be bound to one alone."

sentences.zh: 宋武帝起義兵，累遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised righteous troops, Xianzhi was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu raised righteous troops, Xianzhi rose to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，甚得司直之體。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and straight and very obtained the substance of the upright censor.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was stern and straight, very the upright censor's substance.

sentences.zh: 外甥劉毅權重當時，朝野莫不歸附，鮮之盡心武帝，獨不屈意於毅，毅甚恨焉。

translations.literal: His nephew Liu Yi held heavy power at the time; court and country all attached—Xianzhi devoted his heart to Emperor Wu and alone would not bend his intent to Yi; Yi greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Liu Yi held power; court and country attached—Xianzhi devoted himself to Liu Yu and alone would not bend to Yi; Yi resented it.

sentences.zh: 以與毅舅甥制不相糾，使書侍御史丘洹奏彈毅輒宥傳詔羅道盛。

translations.literal: Because as nephew by marriage the system did not mutually impeach, he had the Attendant Censor Qiu Yuan impeach Yi for arbitrarily pardoning the edict-bearer Luo Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because nephew by marriage could not impeach each other, he had Qiu Yuan impeach Yi for pardoning edict-bearer Luo Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 詔無所問。

translations.literal: An edict made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made no inquiry.

sentences.zh: 時新制，長吏以父母疾去官，禁錮三年。

translations.literal: At that time a new regulation: senior officials who left office for parents' illness were barred for three years.
translations.idiomatic: A new regulation: senior officials leaving for parents' illness were barred three years.

sentences.zh: 山陰令沈叔任父疾去職，鮮之因此上議曰：「今省父母之疾而加以罪名，悖義疾理，莫此為大。

translations.literal: The Magistrate of Shanyin Shen Shuren left office for his father's illness; Xianzhi on this account submitted a debate saying, "Now to add guilt for attending parents' illness violates righteousness and injures principle—nothing greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Shen Shuren left for his father's illness; Xianzhi debated: "Adding guilt for attending parents' illness violates righteousness—nothing greater.

sentences.zh: 謂宜從舊，於義為允。

translations.literal: I say it should follow the old—in righteousness it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the old—in righteousness it is fitting.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " It was followed.

sentences.zh: 於是自二品以上，父母及為祖父母后者，墳墓崩毀及疾病，族屬輒去，並不禁錮。

translations.literal: From then on, from second rank upward, for parents and for those succeeding grandparents, tomb collapse and illness—clansmen left at once and all were not barred.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, second rank upward, for parents and grandparents' successors, tomb collapse and illness—clansmen left and none were barred.

sentences.zh: 劉毅當鎮江陵，武帝會于江寧，朝士畢集。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi was to garrison Jiangling, Emperor Wu met at Jiangning; court gentlemen all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi was to garrison Jiangling, Liu Yu met at Jiangning; court gentlemen gathered.

sentences.zh: 毅素好摴蒱，於是會戲。

translations.literal: Yi had always loved chupu; therefore at the meeting they played.
translations.idiomatic: Yi loved chupu; at the meeting they played.

sentences.zh: 帝與毅斂局各得其半，積錢隱人，毅呼帝並之。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Yi gathered the board each taking half; accumulated cash was hidden from others—Yi called the Emperor to merge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Yi each took half the board; cash was hidden—Yi called the emperor to merge.

sentences.zh: 先擲得雉，帝甚不悅，良久乃答之，四坐傾屬。

translations.literal: First cast and got zhi; the Emperor was very displeased; long afterward he answered; the four seats leaned to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Yi first cast zhi; the emperor was displeased; long after he answered; all leaned to watch.

sentences.zh: 既擲得盧，毅意大惡，謂帝曰：「知公不以大坐席與人。

translations.literal: Having cast and got lu, Yi's intent was greatly bad; he told the Emperor, "I know you would not give the great seat to others."
translations.idiomatic: Casting lu, Yi's mood turned foul; he told the emperor, "I know you won't give the great seat to others."

sentences.zh: 」鮮之大喜，徒跣繞床大叫，聲聲相續，毅甚不平，謂之曰：「此鄭君何為者？

translations.literal: " Xianzhi was greatly pleased, barefoot circled the bed shouting, voice following voice; Yi was very displeased and said to him, "What is this Master Zheng doing?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi was delighted, barefoot circled the bed shouting; Yi was displeased: "What is Master Zheng doing?"

sentences.zh: 」無復甥舅之敬。

translations.literal: " No longer nephew-uncle respect.
translations.idiomatic: " No longer nephew-uncle respect.

sentences.zh: 帝少事戎旅，不經涉學，及為宰相，頗慕風流。

translations.literal: The Emperor in youth served in campaigns and had not passed through learning; when he became chief minister he quite admired elegant culture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in youth served in campaigns, untrained in learning; as chief minister he admired elegant culture.

sentences.zh: 時或談論，人皆依違不敢難。

translations.literal: Sometimes in discussion everyone yielded and did not dare dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes in discussion everyone yielded and dared not dispute.

sentences.zh: 鮮之難必切至，未嘗寬假。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's disputing was always cutting to the utmost and never lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's disputing was always cutting, never lenient.

sentences.zh: 與帝言，要須帝理屈，然後置之。

translations.literal: In speaking with the Emperor he must have the Emperor's reason bent before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking with the emperor, he must have the emperor's reason bent before stopping.

sentences.zh: 帝有時慚恧變色，感其輸情，時人謂為「格佞」。

translations.literal: The Emperor sometimes was ashamed and changed color, moved by his yielding feeling; people of the time called it "blocking the sycophant."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sometimes blushed, moved by his honesty; the age called it "blocking the sycophant."

sentences.zh: 十二年，武帝北伐，以為右長史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Emperor Wu marched north and made him Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Liu Yu marched north and made him right chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 鮮之曾祖晉江州長史哲墓在開封，求拜省，帝以騎送之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's great-grandfather's tomb as Jin Chief Clerk of Jiang Province was at Kaifeng; he requested leave to visit and pay respects; the Emperor sent cavalry to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather's tomb as Jin Jiang Province chief clerk was at Kaifeng; he requested leave; the emperor sent cavalry.

translations.literal: On entering Xianyang the Emperor everywhere viewed the old sites of Epang and Weiyang, moved to sorrow; he asked Xianzhi how Qin and Han obtained and lost.
