translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming because he filed no memorials, replaced and reproached him; Zhaoming said, "I did not wish to compete holding the key—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」昭明曆郡皆清勤，常謂人曰：「人生何事須聚畜，一身之外亦復何須。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming through commanderies was all clear and diligent; he often told others, "What in life needs gathering and storing? Beyond the person what further is needed?
translations.idiomatic: " Through commanderies he was clear and diligent; he often said, "What in life needs storing? Beyond the person what is needed?

sentences.zh: 子孫若不才，我聚彼散。

translations.literal: If sons and grandsons are without talent, I gather and they scatter.
translations.idiomatic: If sons lack talent, I gather and they scatter.

sentences.zh: 若能自立，則不如一經。

translations.literal: If they can stand on their own, then better one classic.
translations.idiomatic: If they can stand on their own, better one classic.

sentences.zh: 」故終身一不事產業。

translations.literal: " Therefore all his life he never engaged in property.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore all his life he never engaged in property.

sentences.zh: 中興二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhongxing 2.

sentences.zh: 子子野。

translations.literal: His son Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziye.

sentences.zh: 子野字幾原，生而母魏氏亡，為祖母殷氏所養。

translations.literal: Ziye, styled Jiyuan, was born and his mother Lady Wei died; he was raised by his grandmother Lady Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye, styled Jiyuan, was born and his mother Lady Wei died; his grandmother Lady Yin raised him.

sentences.zh: 殷柔明有文義，以章句授之。

translations.literal: Yin was gentle and bright with literary meaning and by chapter-and-phrase taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was gentle and bright with literary gifts and taught him by chapter and phrase.

sentences.zh: 年九歲，殷氏亡，泣血哀慟，家人異之。

translations.literal: At nine years Lady Yin died; he wept blood and was moved to grief; the household found him strange.
translations.idiomatic: At nine Lady Yin died; he wept blood in grief; the household found him strange.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善屬文，仕齊為江夏王行參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled at composing, and served Qi as staff officer to the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning, wrote well, and served Qi as staff officer to the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on his father's death.

sentences.zh: 初，父寢疾彌年，子野禱請備至，涕泗沾濡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when his father lay ill for a full year, Ziye prayed and petitioned to the utmost, tears and mucus soaking.
translations.idiomatic: When his father lay ill a full year, Ziye prayed to the utmost, tears soaking.

sentences.zh: 父夜夢見其容，旦召視如夢，俄而疾間，以為至孝所感。

translations.literal: His father at night dreamed he saw his face; at dawn he summoned and looked—as in the dream; soon the illness eased—they thought supreme filiality moved it.
translations.idiomatic: His father dreamed his face; at dawn summoned and looked—as in the dream; soon illness eased—supreme filiality, they thought.

sentences.zh: 命著孝感傳，固辭乃止。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compose the Filiality Moved Biography; he firmly declined and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compose the Filiality Moved Biography; he declined and stopped.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，每之墓所，草為之枯。

translations.literal: When in mourning, each time at the tomb place the grass withered for it.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning, each visit to the tomb the grass withered.

sentences.zh: 有白兔白鳩馴擾其側。

translations.literal: There were white rabbits and white doves tame and lingering at the side.
translations.idiomatic: White rabbits and white doves lingered tame at the side.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，尚書僕射范雲嘉其至行，將表奏之，會雲卒不果。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian of Liang, the Vice Director Fan Yun praised his utmost conduct and was about to memorialize and present it; Yun died and it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang Tianjian's start Vice Director Fan Yun praised his conduct and was about to memorialize; Yun died and it did not happen.

sentences.zh: 樂安任昉有盛名，為後進所慕，遊其門者，昉必推薦。

translations.literal: Le'an Ren Fang had great fame and was admired by the rising generation; those who visited his gate—Fang always recommended them.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang of Le'an had great fame; those who visited his gate—Fang always recommended them.

sentences.zh: 子野於昉為從中表，獨不至，昉亦恨焉，故不之善。

translations.literal: Ziye to Fang was cousin among cousins and alone did not go; Fang also resented it and therefore did not speak well of him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye to Fang was cousin among cousins and alone did not go; Fang resented it and did not speak well.

sentences.zh: 久之兼廷尉正，時三官通署獄，子野嘗不在，同僚輒署其名。

translations.literal: After long time he concurrently was Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review; at that time the three offices jointly handled prison cases—Ziye was sometimes absent and colleagues then signed his name.
translations.idiomatic: After long time he was corrector of judicial review; the three offices jointly handled cases—Ziye absent, colleagues signed his name.

sentences.zh: 奏有不允，子野從坐免職。

translations.literal: When the memorial was not approved, Ziye was implicated and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was not approved, Ziye was implicated and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 或勸言請有司，可無咎，子野笑曰：「雖慚柳季之道，豈因訟以受服。

translations.literal: Some urged speaking to the responsible officials—there could be no blame; Ziye laughed and said, "Though ashamed before Liu Ji's way, how take lawsuit to receive punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged appealing to officials—no blame; Ziye laughed: "Though ashamed before Liu Ji's way, how take lawsuit for punishment."

sentences.zh: 」自此免黜久之，終無恨意。

translations.literal: " From then he was dismissed long and in the end had no resentful intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Dismissed long, in the end no resentful intent.

sentences.zh: 中書郎範縝與子野未遇，聞其行業而善焉。

translations.literal: The Gentleman of the Secretariat Fan Zhen and Ziye had not met; hearing his conduct he approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen of the secretariat and Ziye had not met; hearing his conduct he approved.

sentences.zh: 會遷國子博士，乃上表讓之，有司以資歷非次，不為通。

translations.literal: When transferred to Erudite of the National University he submitted a memorial yielding to Ziye; the responsible officials because qualification was out of order did not pass it.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to national university erudite he yielded to Ziye; officials because qualification was out of order did not pass.

sentences.zh: 後為諸暨令，在縣不行鞭罰，人有爭者，示之以理，百姓稱悅，合境無訟。

translations.literal: Later he was Magistrate of Zhuji; in the county he did not use whip punishment—when people disputed he showed them principle; the common people praised and delighted, the whole territory without lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Later magistrate of Zhuji; he used no whip—when people disputed he showed principle; the people praised, the whole territory without lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 初，子野曾祖松之，宋元嘉中受詔續修何承天宋史，未成而卒，子野常欲繼成先業。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ziye's great-grandfather Songzhi in Yuanjia of Song received edict to continue and revise He Chengtian's Song History; before completion he died—Ziye always wished to continue and complete the former work.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye's great-grandfather Songzhi in Song Yuanjia received edict to continue He Chengtian's Song History; before completion he died—Ziye always wished to continue.

sentences.zh: 及齊永明末，沈約所撰宋書稱「松之已後無聞焉」。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming of Qi, Shen Yue's compiled Song Book said, "After Songzhi there was no report."
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Yongming's end Shen Yue's Song Book said, "After Songzhi there was no report."

sentences.zh: 子野更撰為宋略二十卷，其敘事評論多善，而云：「戮淮南太守沈璞，以其不從義師故也」。

translations.literal: Ziye again compiled it as Song Outline in twenty scrolls; its narrative and commentaries were mostly good, and he said, "Executed Huainan Administrator Shen Pu because he would not follow the righteous army."
translations.idiomatic: Ziye compiled Song Outline in twenty scrolls; narrative and commentaries mostly good, saying, "Executed Huainan governor Shen Pu because he would not follow the righteous army."

sentences.zh: 約懼，徒跣謝之，請兩釋焉。

translations.literal: Yue feared, went barefoot and apologized, requesting mutual release.
translations.idiomatic: Yue feared, went barefoot and apologized, requesting mutual release.

sentences.zh: 歎其述作曰：「吾弗逮也。

translations.literal: He sighed at his writing and said, "I do not reach him."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed at the writing: "I do not reach him."

sentences.zh: 」蘭陵蕭琛言其評論可與過秦、王命分路揚鑣。

translations.literal: " Lanling Xiao Chen said his commentaries could share the road with "Discourse on Qin" and "Royal Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: " Lanling Xiao Chen said his commentaries could share the road with "Discourse on Qin" and "Royal Mandate."

sentences.zh: 於是吏部尚書徐勉言之于武帝，以為著作郎，掌修國史及起居注。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Minister of Personnel Xu Mian told Emperor Wu and he was made Compiler, in charge of revising the national history and the records of attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Xu Mian told the emperor; he was made compiler, revising national history and attendance records.

sentences.zh: 頃之，兼中書通事舍人，尋除通直員外，著作、舍人如故。

translations.literal: Soon he additionally was Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat, removed as Direct Attendant; compiler and attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon additionally supernumerary secretariat attendant-in-ordinary, removed as direct attendant; compiler and attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 敕又掌中書詔誥。

translations.literal: By edict he again was in charge of secretariat edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he again was in charge of secretariat edicts.

sentences.zh: 時西北遠邊有白題及滑國遣使由岷山道入貢，此二國歷代弗賓，莫知所出。

translations.literal: At that time on the far northwest frontier the Baiti and Huaguo sent envoys through the Minshan route to offer tribute—these two states through dynasties had not submitted and none knew whence they came.
translations.idiomatic: On the far northwest frontier Baiti and Huaguo sent envoys through Minshan to tribute—through dynasties unsubmitted, none knew whence.

sentences.zh: 子野曰：「漢潁陰侯斬胡白題將一人。

translations.literal: Ziye said, "Han Marquis of Yingyin beheaded one Baiti general.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye said, "Han Marquis of Yingyin beheaded one Baiti general.

sentences.zh: 服虔注云：'白題，胡名也。

translations.literal: Fu Qian's note says: 'Baiti, Hu name.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian's note: 'Baiti, Hu name.'"

sentences.zh: '又漢定遠侯擊虜，八滑從之，此其後乎。

translations.literal: Again Han Marquis Who Settles the Far Frontier attacked the barbarians—eight Huaguo followed; this is probably their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Again Han Marquis Who Settles the Far Frontier attacked barbarians—eight Huaguo followed; probably their descendants.

sentences.zh: 」時人服其博識。

translations.literal: " People of the time submitted to his broad knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: " The age submitted to his broad knowledge.

sentences.zh: 敕仍使撰方國使圖，廣述懷來之盛，自要服至於海表，凡二十國。

translations.literal: By edict he was again ordered to compile the Map of Frontier Envoys, broadly setting forth the splendor of those who came with hearts bound; from the inner garments to beyond the sea, altogether twenty states.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he compiled the Map of Frontier Envoys, setting forth those who came with hearts bound; from inner garments to beyond the sea, twenty states.

sentences.zh: 子野與沛國劉顯、南陽劉之遴、陳郡殷芸、陳留阮孝緒、吳郡顧協、京兆韋棱皆博學，深相賞好，顯尤推重之。

translations.literal: Ziye with Liu Xian of Pei, Liu Zhixun of Nanyang, Yin Yun of Chen, Ruan Xiaoxu of Chenliu, Gu Xie of Wu, and Wei Leng of Jingzhao were all broadly learned; they deeply admired and befriended one another—Xian especially pushed and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye with Liu Xian, Liu Zhixun, Yin Yun, Ruan Xiaoxu, Gu Xie, and Wei Leng were all broadly learned; they deeply befriended one another—Xian especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 時吳平侯蕭勱、范陽張纘每討論墳籍，咸折衷於子野。

translations.literal: At that time the Marquis of Wu Ping Xiao Xun and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang whenever they discussed the classics all took the middle from Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Xiao Xun of Wu Ping and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, discussing classics, all took the middle from Ziye.

sentences.zh: 繼母曹氏亡，居喪過禮，服闋，再遷員外郎。

translations.literal: When his stepmother Lady Cao died he observed mourning beyond ritual; when mourning ended he was again promoted to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When stepmother Lady Cao died he mourned beyond ritual; when mourning ended, again regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 普通七年，大舉北侵，敕子野為移魏文，受詔立成。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Putong the great northern campaign was raised; by edict Ziye was to compose the letter moving Wei; receiving the command he finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: Putong 7 the great northern campaign; by edict Ziye composed the letter moving Wei; receiving command he finished at once.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其事體大，召尚書僕射徐勉、太子詹事周舍、鴻臚卿劉之遴、中書侍郎朱異集壽光殿以觀之，時並嘆服。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu because the affair's body was great summoned Vice Director Xu Mian, Grand Tutor of the Heir Zhou She, Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Zhixun, and Gentleman of the Secretariat Zhu Yi to gather at Shouguang Hall to view it—at the time all sighed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor because the affair was great summoned Xu Mian, Zhou She, Liu Zhixun, and Zhu Yi to Shouguang Hall—all sighed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 武帝目子野曰：「其形雖弱，其文甚壯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu looked at Ziye and said, "His form though weak, his writing very strong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at Ziye: "His form though weak, his writing very strong."

sentences.zh: 」俄又敕為書喻魏相元叉。

translations.literal: " Soon again by edict a letter instructing Wei's chief minister Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon again by edict a letter instructing Wei's chief minister Yuan Cha.

sentences.zh: 其夜受旨，子野謂可待旦方奏，未之為也，及五鼓，敕催令速上。

translations.literal: That night receiving the command, Ziye said it could wait until dawn before presenting and did not do it; at the fifth drum the edict urged speed.
translations.idiomatic: That night receiving command, Ziye said it could wait until dawn; at fifth drum the edict urged speed.

sentences.zh: 子野徐起操筆，昧爽便就。

translations.literal: Ziye slowly rose, took up the brush; at daybreak it was done.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye slowly rose, took up the brush; at daybreak it was done.

sentences.zh: 及奏，武帝深嘉焉。

translations.literal: On presenting, Emperor Wu deeply praised it.
translations.idiomatic: On presenting, the emperor deeply praised it.

sentences.zh: 自是諸符檄皆令具草。

translations.literal: From then all talismans and proclamations were ordered fully drafted by him.
translations.idiomatic: From then all talismans and proclamations were fully drafted by him.

sentences.zh: 子野為文典而速，不尚靡麗，制多法古，與今文體異。

translations.literal: Ziye's writing was canonical and swift, not admiring ornate beauty; his style mostly followed the ancients and differed from present writing.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye's writing was canonical and swift, not ornate; style mostly followed ancients and differed from present writing.

sentences.zh: 當時或有詆訶者，及其末，翕然重之。

translations.literal: At the time some slandered him; by his end all suddenly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some slandered him; by his end all valued him.

sentences.zh: 或問其為文速者，子野答云：「人皆成於手，我獨成於心。」

translations.literal: When asked about his swift writing, Ziye answered, "Others all accomplish with the hand—I alone accomplish with the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about swift writing, Ziye answered, "Others accomplish with the hand—I alone with the heart."

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎、鴻臚卿，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat and Grand Master of Ceremonies, concurrently Commandant of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretariat gentleman and grand master of ceremonies, concurrently commandant of the footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 子野在禁省十餘年，默靜自守，未嘗有所請謁。

translations.literal: Ziye in the forbidden offices more than ten years was silent and guarded himself and never had requests or visits.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye in forbidden offices more than ten years was silent and guarded, never requesting or visiting.

sentences.zh: 外家及中表貧乏，所得奉悉給之。

translations.literal: Maternal kin and cousins among cousins were poor; all salary received he gave to them.
translations.idiomatic: Maternal kin and cousins were poor; all salary he gave them.

sentences.zh: 無宅，借官地二畝，起茅屋數間，妻子恒苦饑寒，唯以教誨為本，子侄祗畏，若奉嚴君。

translations.literal: He had no house, borrowed two mu of official land, raised several thatched rooms; wife and children always suffered hunger and cold—only teaching was the root; sons and nephews revered him as if serving a strict lord.
translations.idiomatic: No house, borrowed two mu official land, raised thatched rooms; wife and children suffered hunger and cold—only teaching was root; sons and nephews revered him as strict lord.

sentences.zh: 劉顯常以師道推高之。

translations.literal: Liu Xian always by teacher's way pushed him high.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian always by teacher's way pushed him high.

sentences.zh: 末年深信釋教，終身飯麥食蔬。

translations.literal: In his later years he deeply believed in Buddhist teaching and all his life ate wheat and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he deeply believed Buddhism and all life ate wheat and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Zhongtong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhongtong 2.

sentences.zh: 先是，子野自占死期不過庚戌歲，是年自省移疾，謂同官劉之亨曰：「吾其逝矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ziye himself divined that the term of death would not pass the gengxu year; that year he himself reported illness, telling colleague Liu Zhiheng, "I am about to depart."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ziye divined death would not pass gengxu year; that year he reported illness, telling Liu Zhiheng, "I am about to depart."

sentences.zh: 」遺命務存儉約。

translations.literal: " Final orders insisted on remaining frugal.
translations.idiomatic: " Final orders insisted on frugality.

sentences.zh: 武帝悼惜，為之流涕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu mourned and prized him and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍，即日舉哀。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Supernumerary Regular Attendant; mourning was raised that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously supernumerary regular attendant; mourning raised that same day.

sentences.zh: 先是，五等君及侍中以上乃有諡，及子野特以令望見嘉，賜諡貞子。

translations.literal: Earlier, fifth-rank lords and attendant-in-ordinary and above then had posthumous titles; for Ziye specially because of fine reputation he was praised and granted the posthumous title Lord Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier fifth-rank lords and attendant-in-ordinary and above had posthumous titles; for Ziye specially for fine reputation granted posthumous title Lord Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子野少時集注喪服、續裴氏家傳各二卷，抄合後漢事四十餘卷。

translations.literal: In youth Ziye collected and annotated Mourning Garments and continued the Pei Family Genealogy two scrolls each, and copied and combined Later Han affairs in more than forty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ziye annotated Mourning Garments and continued the Pei Family Genealogy two scrolls each, copied Later Han affairs forty-plus scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又敕撰眾僧傳二十卷，百官九品二卷，附益諡法一卷，方國使圖一卷，文集二十卷：並行於世。

translations.literal: Again by edict he compiled Biographies of Many Monks in twenty scrolls, Ranks of the Hundred Offices in nine ranks two scrolls, supplementary posthumous titles one scroll, Map of Frontier Envoys one scroll, collected works twenty scrolls—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Again by edict Biographies of Many Monks twenty scrolls, Ranks of the Hundred Offices two scrolls, supplementary posthumous titles one scroll, Map of Frontier Envoys one scroll, collected works twenty scrolls—all circulated.

sentences.zh: 又欲撰齊梁春秋，始草創，未就而卒。

translations.literal: Again he wished to compile Qi-Liang Spring and Autumn; he first drafted but before completion died.
translations.idiomatic: Again he wished to compile Qi-Liang Spring and Autumn; first drafted but before completion died.

sentences.zh: 及葬，湘東王為之墓誌銘，陳于藏內。

translations.literal: At burial the Prince of Xiangdong composed the tomb inscription and displayed it in the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At burial the Prince of Xiangdong composed the tomb inscription and displayed it in the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王又立墓誌，堙於羨道。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shaoling again set up a tomb inscription and buried it in the spirit path.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shaoling again set a tomb inscription and buried it in the spirit path.

sentences.zh: 羨道列志，自此始焉。

translations.literal: Spirit-path array of records—from this it began.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-path array of records—from this it began.

sentences.zh: 子騫，官至通直郎。

translations.literal: His son Qian reached Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian reached direct attendant.

sentences.zh: 何承天，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: He Chengtian was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian was from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 五歲喪父。

translations.literal: At five he lost his father.
translations.idiomatic: At five he lost his father.

sentences.zh: 母徐廣姊也，聰明博學，故承天幼漸訓義。

translations.literal: His mother was elder sister to Xu Guang, intelligent and broadly learned—therefore Chengtian from youth gradually received instruction in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Xu Guang's elder sister, intelligent and learned—Chengtian from youth received instruction in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 宋武起義初，撫軍將軍劉毅鎮姑孰，板為行參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song Wu's righteous rising, the General Who Pacifies the Army Liu Yi garrisoned Gushu and appointed him as traveling staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu Yu's righteous rising, Liu Yi garrisoned Gushu and appointed him traveling staff officer.

sentences.zh: 毅嘗出行，而鄢陵縣吏陳滿射鳥，箭誤中直帥，雖不傷人，處法棄市。

translations.literal: Yi once went out, and the Yiling county clerk Chen Man shot birds; the arrow mistakenly hit the straight guard; though it did not harm a person, by law he was abandoned to the market.
translations.idiomatic: Yi once went out; Yiling county clerk Chen Man shot birds; the arrow mistakenly hit the straight guard; though no harm, by law abandoned to the market.

sentences.zh: 承天議曰：「獄貴情斷，疑則從輕。

translations.literal: Chengtian debated, saying, "In prison what is prized is judging by feeling; in doubt follow the lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian debated: "In prison what is prized is judging by feeling; in doubt follow the lighter.

sentences.zh: 昔有驚漢文帝乘輿馬者，張釋之劾以犯蹕，罪止罰金。

translations.literal: Formerly there was one who startled Emperor Wen of Han's carriage horse; Zhang Shizhi impeached him for violating the imperial progress—punishment stopped at fine gold.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly one startled Emperor Wen of Han's carriage horse; Zhang Shizhi impeached for violating the progress—punishment stopped at fine.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 明其無心于驚馬也。

translations.literal: It showed he had no heart to startle the horse.
translations.idiomatic: It showed he had no heart to startle the horse.

sentences.zh: 故不以乘輿之重，加於異制。

translations.literal: Therefore the weight of the imperial carriage was not added with a different measure.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the imperial carriage's weight was not added with different measure.

sentences.zh: 今滿意在射鳥，非有心于中人。

translations.literal: Now Man's intent was in shooting birds—not having heart to hit a person.
translations.idiomatic: Now Man's intent was shooting birds—not heart to hit a person.

sentences.zh: 案律過誤傷人三歲刑，況不傷乎？

translations.literal: According to law, accidental injury to a person is three years' punishment—how much more when there is no injury?
translations.idiomatic: By law accidental injury is three years—how much more when no injury?

sentences.zh: 微罰可也。」

translations.literal: A light punishment can suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Light punishment suffices."

sentences.zh: 宋台建，為尚書祠部郎，與傅亮共撰朝儀。

translations.literal: When the Song court was established he was Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Rites and with Fu Liang jointly compiled court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song court was established he was senior clerk of rites and with Fu Liang compiled court ritual.

sentences.zh: 謝晦鎮江陵，請為南蠻長史。

translations.literal: Xie Hui garrisoned Jiangling and requested him as senior administrator of the Southern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui garrisoned Jiangling and requested him as senior administrator of the southern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 晦進號衛將軍，轉諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: Hui advanced in title to General Who Guards the Army and was transferred to staff adviser, concurrently recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Hui advanced to general who guards the army and was transferred to staff adviser, recorder.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，晦將見討，間計於承天，曰：「大小既殊，逆順又異，境外求全，上計也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia Hui was about to be punished; he asked Chengtian for plan and said, "Great and small are already different, rebellious and compliant also differ—seeking completeness outside the border is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 3 Hui was about to be punished; he asked Chengtian: "Great and small differ, rebellious and compliant differ—seeking completeness outside the border is upper plan.

sentences.zh: 以腹心領兵戍義陽，將軍率眾于夏口一戰。

translations.literal: With trusted men lead troops to garrison Yiyang; the general leads the multitude in one battle at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: With trusted men garrison Yiyang; the general leads troops in one battle at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 若敗，即趨義陽，以出北境，此其次也。

translations.literal: If defeated, then hurry to Yiyang and exit the northern border—this is the second.
translations.idiomatic: If defeated, hurry to Yiyang and exit the northern border—second.

sentences.zh: 」晦良久曰：「荊楚用武之國，且當決戰，走不晚也。

translations.literal: " Hui long said, "Jing-Chu is a land of using arms—and one should decide battle; fleeing is not late."
translations.idiomatic: " Hui long said, "Jing-Chu is a land of arms—decide battle; fleeing is not late."

sentences.zh: 」及晦下，承天留府不從。

translations.literal: When Hui fell Chengtian remained at the prefecture and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui fell Chengtian remained at the prefecture and did not follow.

sentences.zh: 到彥之至馬頭，承天自詣歸罪，見宥。

translations.literal: When Dao Yanzhi reached Matou, Chengtian went himself to confess guilt and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao Yanzhi reached Matou, Chengtian confessed guilt and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Later he additionally was Senior Clerk of the Ministry of the Interior on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Later additionally senior clerk of the interior on the left.

sentences.zh: 吳興余杭人薄道舉為劫，制同籍期親補兵。

translations.literal: Bo Daoju of Yuhang in Wuxing was a robber; the regulation was same-register close-kin conscript soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Daoju of Yuhang in Wuxing was a robber; regulation was same-register close-kin conscript soldiers.

sentences.zh: 道舉從弟代公、道生等並為劫大功親，非應在補謫之例。

translations.literal: Daoju's younger cousins from father's side Daigong, Daosheng, and others were all robbers of great-merit kin—not fitting the example of supplementary exile.
translations.idiomatic: Daoju's younger cousins Daigong, Daosheng were robbers of great-merit kin—not fitting supplementary exile.

sentences.zh: 法以代公等母存為期親，則子宜隨母補兵。

translations.literal: Law because Daigong and others' mother lived made them close-kin—then sons should follow mother to supplementary soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Law because their mother lived made them close-kin—sons should follow mother to supplementary soldiers.

sentences.zh: 承天議曰：「尋劫制，同籍期親補兵，大功則不在此例。

translations.literal: Chengtian debated, saying, "Examining robbery regulation, same-register close-kin supplementary soldiers—great merit is not in this example.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian debated: "Robbery regulation: same-register close-kin supplementary soldiers—great merit not in this example.

sentences.zh: 婦人三從，既嫁從夫，夫死從子。

translations.literal: Women have three followings: having married they follow the husband; husband dead they follow the son.
translations.idiomatic: Women have three followings: married follow husband; husband dead follow son.

sentences.zh: 今道舉為劫，若其叔父尚存，制應補謫，妻子營居，固其宜也。

translations.literal: Now Daoju was robber—if his father's younger brother still lived, by regulation supplementary exile should apply, wife and children maintaining residence—that is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Now Daoju was robber—if father's younger brother lived, supplementary exile should apply, wife and children maintaining residence—fitting.

sentences.zh: 但為劫之時，叔父已歿，代公、道生並是從弟，大功之親，不合補謫。

translations.literal: But at the time of robbery the father's younger brother had already died; Daigong and Daosheng are all younger cousins—great-merit kin, not fitting supplementary exile.
translations.idiomatic: But at robbery father's younger brother had died; Daigong and Daosheng are younger cousins—great-merit kin, not fitting exile.

sentences.zh: 今若以叔母為期親，令代公隨母補兵，既乖大功不謫之制，又失婦人三從之道。

translations.literal: Now if because the father's younger brother's wife is close-kin one makes Daigong follow mother to supplementary soldiers—it both violates the regulation that great merit is not exiled and loses the woman's three-followings way.
translations.idiomatic: If because the uncle's wife is close-kin one makes Daigong follow mother to soldiers—it violates great-merit non-exile and loses three followings.

sentences.zh: 由於主者守期親之文，不辨男女之異。

translations.literal: This is because the responsible ones hold the close-kin text and do not distinguish male and female difference.
translations.idiomatic: Responsible ones hold close-kin text and do not distinguish male and female.

sentences.zh: 謂代公等母子並宜見原。」

translations.literal: I say Daigong and others, mother and sons—all should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Daigong and others, mother and sons—all should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 承天為性剛愎，不能屈意朝右，頗以所長侮同列，不為僕射殷景仁所平。

translations.literal: Chengtian by nature was stern and obstinate and could not bend his intent to court superiors; he quite by what he was skilled at insulted colleagues and was not approved by the Vice Director Yin Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian by nature was stern and obstinate, could not bend to superiors; he insulted colleagues by his specialties and Yin Jingren did not approve.

sentences.zh: 出為衡陽內史。

translations.literal: He went out as Internal Administrator of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as internal administrator of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 昔在西方與士人多不協，在郡又不公清，為州司所糾，被收系獄，會赦免。

translations.literal: Formerly in the west he was mostly not in harmony with scholars; in the commandery again he was not fair and clear and was impeached by the provincial inspector, taken and imprisoned; he met amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in the west he was mostly not in harmony with scholars; in the commandery again not fair and clear, impeached by provincial inspector, imprisoned; amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，除著作佐郎，撰國史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was made Assistant Compiler and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was assistant compiler and compiled national history.

sentences.zh: 承天年已老，而諸佐郎並名家年少。

translations.literal: Chengtian's years were already old, yet all assistant compilers were famous-house youths.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian was already old, yet all assistant compilers were famous-house youths.

sentences.zh: 潁川荀伯子嘲之，常呼為奶母。

translations.literal: Yingchuan Xun Bozi mocked him and always called him wet-nurse.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Bozi mocked him and always called him wet-nurse.

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「卿當云鳳凰將九子，奶母何言邪？

translations.literal: Chengtian said, "You ought to say the phoenix will have nine sons—what talk of wet-nurse?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian said, "You ought to say the phoenix will have nine sons—what talk of wet-nurse?"

sentences.zh: 」尋轉太子率更令，著作如故。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Rate Regulation, compiler as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon commandant of the heir's rate regulation, compiler as before.

sentences.zh: 時丹陽溧陽丁況等久喪而不棺葬，承天議曰：「禮雲'還葬'，當謂荒儉一時，故許其稱財而不求備。

translations.literal: At that time in Danyang Liyang Ding Kuang and others long mourned yet did not coffin and bury; Chengtian debated, saying, "Ritual says 'return and bury'—this should mean wasteland and frugality for a time, therefore permitting according to resources and not seeking completeness.
translations.idiomatic: In Danyang Liyang Ding Kuang and others long mourned yet did not coffin; Chengtian debated: "Ritual 'return and bury' means wasteland frugality for a time, permitting according to resources.

sentences.zh: 丁況三家數年中葬輒無棺櫬，實由淺情薄恩同於禽獸者耳。

translations.literal: Ding Kuang's three households for several years at burial always had no coffin—truly because shallow feeling and thin grace were the same as birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Kuang's three households for years at burial had no coffin—shallow feeling and thin grace same as beasts.

sentences.zh: 竊以丁寶等同伍積年，未嘗勸之以義，繩之以法。

translations.literal: I privately think Ding Bao and others of the same ward for accumulated years never urged them with righteousness or bound them with law.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Bao and others of the same ward for years never urged with righteousness or bound with law.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，既無新科，又未申明舊制，有何嚴切，欻然相糾。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year winter there was neither new statute nor declaration of old system—what strictness, suddenly mutually impeaching?
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth year winter neither new statute nor old declared—what strictness, suddenly impeaching?

sentences.zh: 或由鄰曲分爭，以興此言。

translations.literal: Perhaps because neighbors disputed and on this account arose these words.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps neighbors disputed and arose these words.

sentences.zh: 如聞在東諸處，此例既多，江西、淮北尤為不少。

translations.literal: As heard in eastern places this example is already many; Jiangxi and north of the Huai especially not few.
translations.idiomatic: In eastern places this example is many; Jiangxi and north of the Huai especially not few.

sentences.zh: 若但謫此三人，殆無所肅，開其一端，則互相恐動。

translations.literal: If only these three households are exiled, probably nothing will be awed; opening one end, then mutually frightening one another.
translations.idiomatic: If only these three are exiled, probably nothing awed; opening one end, mutually frightening.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂況等三家，且可勿問，因此附定制旨：若人葬不如法，同伍當即糾言。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks Kuang's three households for the time can be not inquired; thereby attaching fixed regulation: if people bury not according to law, same ward should at once impeach and speak.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's three households for now can be not inquired; attach fixed regulation: if bury not according to law, same ward should impeach.

sentences.zh: 三年除服之後，不得追相告引。」

translations.literal: After three years when mourning garments are removed, one must not pursue mutual citation."
translations.idiomatic: After three years when mourning removed, no mutual citation."

sentences.zh: 十九年，立國子學，以本官領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the National University was established; by original office he was Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth year the National University was established; by original office he was director.

sentences.zh: 皇太子講孝經，承天與中庶子顏延之同為執經。

translations.literal: The crown prince lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; Chengtian with the Attendant Yan Yanzhi together held the classic.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; Chengtian with Yan Yanzhi held the classic.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時魏軍南伐，文帝訪群臣捍禦之略。

translations.literal: At that time Wei armies marched south to attack; Emperor Wen consulted ministers on strategies to defend and resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wei armies marched south; Emperor Wen consulted ministers on defense.

sentences.zh: 承天上安邊論，凡陳四事：其一，移遠就近，以實內地；

translations.literal: Chengtian submitted Secure the Frontier Discourse, altogether stating four matters: first, move distant near to fill the inner lands;
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian submitted Secure the Frontier Discourse, four matters: first, move distant near to fill inner lands;

sentences.zh: 其二，浚復城隍，以增阻防；

translations.literal: second, dredge and restore walls and moats to increase barriers;
translations.idiomatic: second, dredge walls and moats to increase barriers;

sentences.zh: 其三，纂偶車牛，以飾戎械；

translations.literal: third, gather paired oxen and carts to equip military gear;
translations.idiomatic: third, gather paired oxen and carts to equip military gear;

sentences.zh: 其四，計丁課仗，勿使有闕。

translations.literal: fourth, count households and levy weapons, do not let there be lack.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, count households and levy weapons, let none lack.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text mostly is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The text mostly is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 承天素好弈棋，頗用廢事。

translations.literal: Chengtian by nature loved playing go and quite by this neglected affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian loved go and quite neglected affairs.

sentences.zh: 又善彈箏。

translations.literal: Again he was skilled at plucking the zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Again skilled at plucking the zheng.

sentences.zh: 文帝賜以局子及銀裝箏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen granted him go stones and a silver-mounted zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen granted go stones and a silver-mounted zheng.

sentences.zh: 承天奉表陳謝，上答曰：「局子之賜，何必非張武之金邪。」

translations.literal: Chengtian submitted a memorial of thanks; the Emperor replied, "The grant of go stones—how must it not be Zhang Wu's gold?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian submitted thanks; the emperor replied, "Go stones—how must it not be Zhang Wu's gold?"

sentences.zh: 承天博見古今，為一時所重。

translations.literal: Chengtian broadly saw ancient and modern and was valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian broadly saw ancient and modern and was valued by the age.

sentences.zh: 張永嘗開玄武湖遇古塚，塚上得一銅鬥，有柄。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong once opened Xuanwu Lake and encountered an ancient tomb; on the tomb was obtained a bronze ladle with handle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong once opened Xuanwu Lake and found an ancient tomb; on it a bronze ladle with handle.

sentences.zh: 文帝以訪朝士。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen by it consulted court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen consulted court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「此亡新威鬥。

translations.literal: Chengtian said, "This is the authority-ladle of doomed Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian said, "This is doomed Xin's authority-ladle.

sentences.zh: 王莽三公亡，皆賜之。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang's three dukes died, all were granted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang's three dukes died, all were granted them.

sentences.zh: 一在塚外，一在塚內。

translations.literal: One outside the tomb, one inside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: One outside the tomb, one inside.

sentences.zh: 時三台居江左者，唯甄邯為大司徒，必邯之墓。

translations.literal: At that time of the Three Excellencies dwelling in the east only Zhen Han was Grand Minister of Works—it must be Han's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Three Excellencies in the east only Zhen Han was grand minister of works—it must be Han's tomb.

sentences.zh: 」俄而永又啟塚內更得一斗，復有一石銘「大司徒甄邯之墓」。

translations.literal: " Soon Yong again reported inside the tomb another ladle obtained, again a stone inscription 'Tomb of Grand Minister of Works Zhen Han.'
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Yong reported another ladle inside, stone inscription 'Tomb of Grand Minister of Works Zhen Han.'"

sentences.zh: 時帝每有疑議，必先訪之，信命相望於道。

translations.literal: At that time whenever the Emperor had doubtful matters he always first consulted him; letters of trust and command followed one another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor had doubts he consulted Chengtian first; letters of trust followed on the road.

sentences.zh: 承天性褊促，嘗對主者厲聲曰：「天何言哉，四時行焉，百物生焉。

translations.literal: Chengtian by nature was narrow and quick; he once facing the responsible one said in fierce voice, "Heaven what words? Four seasons move, the hundred things are born."
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian was narrow and quick; once facing the responsible one he said fiercely, "Heaven what words? Four seasons move, hundred things are born."

sentences.zh: 」文帝知之，應遣先戒曰：「善候何顏色，如其不悅，無須多陳。」

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen knowing it, when sending always first warned, saying, "Well observe He's countenance; if he is not pleased, need not speak much."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen knowing, when sending always warned first: "Observe He's countenance; if not pleased, speak little."

sentences.zh: 二十四年，承天遷廷尉，未拜，上欲以為吏部郎，已受密旨，承天宣漏之，坐免官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Chengtian was transferred to Minister of Justice; before accepting appointment the Emperor wished to make him Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel; having already received secret command, Chengtian leaked it and on account was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-fourth year Chengtian was transferred to minister of justice; before accepting the emperor wished him senior clerk of personnel; having received secret command, Chengtian leaked it and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died at home, age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, age seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 先是禮論有八百卷，承天刪減併合，以類相從，凡為三百卷，並前傳、雜語、所纂文及文集，並傳於世。

translations.literal: Earlier Ritual Discourse had eight hundred scrolls; Chengtian deleted, reduced, and merged by category, altogether three hundred scrolls, together with former commentary, miscellaneous words, compiled writings and collected works—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ritual Discourse had eight hundred scrolls; Chengtian deleted and merged to three hundred, with commentary, miscellaneous words, writings and collected works—all circulated.

sentences.zh: 又改定元嘉曆，改漏刻用二十五箭，皆從之。

translations.literal: Again he revised the Yuanjia calendar, revised clepsydra to use twenty-five arrows—all followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Again he revised the Yuanjia calendar, clepsydra to twenty-five arrows—all followed.

sentences.zh: 曾孫遜。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson Xun.

sentences.zh: 遜字仲言，八歲能賦詩，弱冠，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Zhongyan, at eight could compose poetry; at weak adulthood the province recommended him as Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, styled Zhongyan, at eight composed poetry; at weak adulthood the province recommended outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 南鄉範雲見其對策，大相稱賞，因結忘年交。

translations.literal: Fan Yun of Nanxiang seeing his examination answer greatly praised and valued him and therefore formed a friendship disregarding age.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun of Nanxiang seeing his examination answer greatly praised him and formed a friendship disregarding age.

sentences.zh: 謂所親曰：「頃觀文人，質則過儒，麗則傷俗，其能含清濁，中今古，見之何生矣。

translations.literal: He told those close, "Looking at writers recently, plain then exceeds the ru, ornate then harms the vulgar—he who can hold clear and turbid, middle ancient and modern, seeing him is He Sheng."
translations.idiomatic: He told intimates, "Writers recently, plain exceeds ru, ornate harms vulgar—he who holds clear and turbid, middle ancient and modern, is He Sheng."

sentences.zh: 」沈約嘗謂遜曰：「吾每讀卿詩，一日三復，猶不能已。

translations.literal: " Shen Yue once told Xun, "Each time I read your poetry, three times in a day I still cannot stop."
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Yue told Xun, "Each time I read your poetry, three times a day I still cannot stop."

sentences.zh: 」其為名流所稱如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the praise of famous currents.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was famous praise.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，兼尚書水部郎，南平王引為賓客，掌記室事，後薦之武帝，與吳均俱進幸。

translations.literal: In Tianjian of Liang he additionally was Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Works for Waterways; the Prince of Nanping led him as guest and controlled recorder affairs; later recommended to Emperor Wu—together with Wu Jun both advanced in favor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tianjian additionally senior clerk for waterways; Prince of Nanping led him as guest, controlled recorder affairs; later recommended to the emperor—with Wu Jun both advanced in favor.

sentences.zh: 後稍失意，帝曰：「吳均不均，何遜不遜。

translations.literal: Later gradually displeased, the Emperor said, "Wu Jun not even, He Xun not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Later gradually displeased, the emperor said, "Wu Jun not even, He Xun not deferential.

sentences.zh: 未若吾有朱異，信則異矣。

translations.literal: Better that I have Zhu Yi—trust then differs."
translations.idiomatic: Better I have Zhu Yi—trust then differs."

sentences.zh: 」自是疏隔，希復得見。

translations.literal: From then estranged, seldom again seen.
translations.idiomatic: From then estranged, seldom seen.

sentences.zh: 卒于仁威廬陵王記室。

translations.literal: He died as recorder to the Prince of Luling, Renwei.
translations.idiomatic: He died as recorder to the Prince of Luling, Renwei.

sentences.zh: 初，遜為南平王所知，深被恩禮，及聞遜卒，命迎其柩而殯藏焉，並餼其妻子。

translations.literal: Earlier Xun was known to the Prince of Nanping and deeply received favor and ritual; when hearing Xun died he ordered his coffin brought and temporarily stored and provided for his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was known to the Prince of Nanping and deeply favored; hearing he died the prince ordered the coffin brought and stored and provided for wife and children.

sentences.zh: 東海王僧孺集其文為八卷。

translations.literal: Wang Sengru of Donghai collected his writings in eight scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengru collected his writings in eight scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初，遜文章與劉孝綽並見重，時謂之何、劉。

translations.literal: Earlier Xun's writing and Liu Xiaochuo were both valued; at the time they were called He and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's writing and Liu Xiaochuo were both valued; the age called them He and Liu.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝著論論之云：「詩多而能者沈約，少而能者謝朓、何遜。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang in a treatise discussing them said, "Many in poetry and able is Shen Yue; few in poetry and able are Xie Tiao and He Xun."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang in a treatise said, "Many in poetry and able is Shen Yue; few and able are Xie Tiao and He Xun."

sentences.zh: 遜從叔澗字彥夷，亦以才著聞，宦游不達，作拍張賦以喻意。

translations.literal: Xun's younger cousin from father's side Jian, styled Yanyi, also by talent was renowned; official travel did not succeed and he composed the "Pai Zhang Fu" to express intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's cousin Jian, styled Yanyi, also renowned by talent; office did not succeed and he composed "Pai Zhang Fu" to express intent.

sentences.zh: 末云：「東方曼倩發憤於侏儒，遂與火頭食子稟賜不殊。

translations.literal: The end says, "Dongfang Manqian vented anger at dwarfs and thus with the fire-head eating child received grant without difference."
translations.idiomatic: The end says, "Dongfang Manqian vented anger at dwarfs and with the fire-head eating child received grant without difference."

sentences.zh: 」位至台郎。

translations.literal: " Rank reached Platform Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: " Rank reached platform gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時有會稽虞騫工為五言，名與遜埒，官至王國侍郎。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Qian of Kuaiji was skilled at five-character poetry, fame equal to Xun, rank reached kingdom attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian of Kuaiji was skilled at five-character poetry, fame equal to Xun, rank kingdom attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 後又有會稽孔翁歸、濟陽江避並為南平王大司馬府記室。

translations.literal: Later again Kuaiji Kong Wengui and Jiyang Jiang Bi both were recorders to the Prince of Nanping, grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kuaiji Kong Wengui and Jiyang Jiang Bi both were recorders to the Prince of Nanping, grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 翁歸工為詩，避博學有思理，注論語、孝經。

translations.literal: Wengui was skilled at composing poetry; Bi was broadly learned with thoughtful principle, annotating Analects and Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui skilled at poetry; Bi broadly learned, annotating Analects and Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 二人並有文集。

translations.literal: Both men had collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Both had collected works.

sentences.zh: 論曰：夫令問令望，詩人所以作詠，有禮有法，前哲由斯播美。

translations.literal: Discourse says: Fine reputation and fine expectation—poets therefore make praise; having ritual and having law—former worthies by this spread beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse says: Fine reputation and expectation—poets make praise; ritual and law—worthies spread beauty.

sentences.zh: 觀夫范、荀二公，並以學業自著，而幹時之譽，本期俱不為弘。

translations.literal: Looking at the two lords Fan and Xun, both by learning established themselves and were renowned; yet the reputation of serving the times—in origin both expected not to be great.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Xun both by learning established themselves; yet reputation for serving the times—in origin both expected not great.

sentences.zh: 雖才則有餘而望乃不足。

translations.literal: Though talent had surplus, expectation was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Though talent had surplus, expectation was insufficient.

sentences.zh: 蔚宗藝用有過人之美，跡其行事，何利害之相傾。

translations.literal: Weizong's art and use had beauty surpassing others; tracing his deeds, how profit and harm leaned against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Weizong's art surpassed others; tracing his deeds, how profit and harm leaned against each other.

sentences.zh: 徐廣動不違仁，義兼儒行。

translations.literal: Xu Guang moved without violating benevolence, righteousness joining Confucian conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang moved without violating benevolence, righteousness joining Confucian conduct.

sentences.zh: 鮮之時稱「格佞」，斯不佞矣。

translations.literal: Xianzhi at the time was called "blocking the sycophant"—this is not sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was called "blocking the sycophant"—this is not sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 松之雅道為貴，實光載德。

translations.literal: Songzhi's elegant way was prized—truly he carried virtue in light.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi's elegant way was prized—truly carrying virtue in light.

sentences.zh: 承天素訓所資，無慚舅氏，美矣乎。

translations.literal: Chengtian by plain instruction was endowed—no shame before his maternal uncle; beautiful indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian by plain instruction was endowed—no shame before his maternal uncle; beautiful indeed.
